questions.stem: Clark, a professional tax return preparer, prepared and signed a client's Year 2 federal income tax return that resulted in a $600 refund. Which one of the following statements is correct with regard to an Internal Revenue Code penalty Clark may be subject to for endorsing and cashing the client's refund check?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clark will be subject to the penalty if Clark endorses and cashes the check.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clark may endorse and cash the check, without penalty, if Clark is enrolled to practice before the Internal Revenue Service.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clark will be subject to the penalty if Clark endorses and cashes the check because the check is for more than $500.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clark may endorse and cash the check, without penalty, if the amount does not exceed Clark's fee for preparation of the return.

questions.explanation: Any person, including a CPA, who is a tax return preparer is prohibited from endorsing or negotiating a client's tax refund check. This applies to any tax refund check, regardless of the amount. The penalty for violating this rule is $500 per endorsed check. The penalty's purpose is to ensure tax return preparers do not commingle a client's tax refund with the preparer's funds.
questions.explanationJa: 税務申告書作成者は、CPAであるかどうかにかかわらず、顧客の還付小切手に裏書きしたり換金したりすることを禁じられている。この禁止は還付額の大小に関係なく適用されるため、$600という金額や作成報酬との比較、IRSへの登録の有無は結論を左右しない。違反した場合のペナルティは裏書きした小切手1枚につき$500である。この規定は、顧客の還付金と作成者自身の資金が混ざるのを防ぐためのものである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.1

questions.stem: A tax preparer has advised a company to take a position on its tax return. The tax preparer believes that there is a 75% possibility that the position will be sustained if audited by the IRS. If the position is not sustained, an accuracy-related penalty and a late-payment penalty would apply. What is the tax preparer's responsibility regarding disclosure of the penalty to the company?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The tax preparer is responsible for disclosing both penalties to the company.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The tax preparer is responsible for disclosing only the accuracy-related penalty to the company.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tax preparer is responsible for disclosing only the late-payment penalty to the company.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tax preparer has no responsibility for disclosing any potential penalties to the company, because the position will probably be sustained on audit.

questions.explanation:
A tax return preparer is required to advise clients of any penalty that is reasonably likely to be assessed against them. As part of this requirement, the preparer (CPA) must also disclose ways to change a client's tax position so the IRS will not assess a penalty.

The penalty disclosure requirement applies for tax positions taken:

Tax returns: On a tax return in which:

The preparer signed or prepared the return, or

Advised the client to take the position on the return.

Other documents: In any document, affidavit, or other paper submitted to the IRS by the CPA.

The purpose of this disclosure rule is to allow taxpayers to make well-informed decisions about any risks associated with tax positions taken on their tax returns.

("The tax preparer is responsible for disclosing only the accuracy-rela…" / "The tax preparer is responsible for disclosing only the late-payment…" / "The tax preparer has no responsibility for disclosing any potential p…") The tax preparer's duty to disclose a potential penalty does not depend on the type of penalty that may apply or the probability of the tax position being sustained on audit.
questions.explanationJa: 申告書作成者は、顧客に課される可能性が合理的に見込まれるペナルティをすべて顧客に助言しなければならず、ペナルティを回避するための申告ポジションの変更方法も示す必要がある。この義務は、作成者が申告書に署名・作成した場合だけでなく、顧客にそのポジションを取るよう助言した場合にも及ぶ。開示義務はペナルティの種類や、税務調査でポジションが認められる確率（本問の75%）には左右されない。したがって、正確性関連ペナルティと延滞納付ペナルティの両方を開示する責任がある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.2

questions.stem: Which of the following would be required to register for a Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A CPA preparing returns in exchange for services but receiving no monetary compensation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A CPA preparing returns for family and friends for no charge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A CPA preparing a return for an entity as an employee of that entity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A CPA's assistant who enters taxpayer data into an electronic tax return preparation system.

questions.explanation:
A tax return preparer includes anyone who prepares for compensation, or who employs one or more persons to prepare, all or a substantial portion of any tax return or claim for refund. The compensation can be either explicit (for money) or implicit (barter). A CPA is not classified as a tax return preparer if the CPA prepares a tax return for a family member or friend free of charge.

Anyone who qualifies as a tax return preparer must obtain a Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN). The PTIN is a nine-digit number that must be used on all the tax returns and claims for refund prepared by the CPA. The PTIN must be renewed annually.

("A CPA preparing a return for an entity as an employee of that entity.") IRS rules specifically exempt from the definition of tax return preparer those employees who, as part of their job, prepare their employer's tax return.

("A CPA's assistant who enters taxpayer data into an electronic tax ret…") Merely entering a taxpayer's data into an electronic tax return preparation system does not qualify a person as a tax return preparer.
questions.explanationJa: 税務申告書作成者とは、報酬を得て申告書や還付請求の全部または大部分を作成する者（またはそれを行う者を雇用する者）をいい、報酬は金銭に限らずサービスの交換（バーター）のような暗黙のものも含む。作成者に該当する者は、毎年更新が必要な9桁のPTINを取得しなければならない。したがって、金銭は受け取らずサービスと引き換えに申告書を作成するCPAはPTINの登録が必要である。家族や友人のために無償で作成する場合、雇用主の申告書を職務として作成する従業員、申告ソフトにデータを入力するだけの補助者は、いずれも作成者に当たらない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.3

questions.stem: Baner, a CPA, is preparing a tax return for Affleck, a new client. During the course of the interview, Baner asks to inspect Affleck's source documents. Affleck responds that the supporting information is not readily available but assures Baner that the summary information is reliable. Which of the following statements best describes how Baner should proceed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Baner cannot accept Affleck's representations. The representations must be verifiable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Baner can accept the representations and explain to Affleck that the IRS's audit coverage is very low.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Baner can automatically accept the representations, because a CPA is under no obligation to verify all client information.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Baner can accept the representations but should make reasonable inquiries to determine if the information appears to be incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent.

questions.explanation:
CPA may, in good faith, rely on information obtained from a client without verification. However, if the information furnished by the client appears incorrect, incomplete, or otherwise unsatisfactory, the CPA cannot ignore it.

The CPA can accept the client and start preparing the tax return based on the client's representation(s) without having to verify every item of information the client provided. However, the CPA must use professional knowledge and judgment to determine if the client's information appears correct or incorrect. Basically, it's a "reasonableness" test. If something in the client's information appears unreasonable or incorrect, the CPA must investigate further by making sensible inquiries to clear up the discrepancies.

For instance, a wealthy client claiming to have only $500 of income for the year, on the surface, doesn't seem plausible. The CPA will need to investigate further (obtain client's tax transcript from the IRS) to determine if the client's claim of only $500 income is true.

("Baner can accept the representations and explain to Affleck that the…") A CPA must investigate discrepancies in a client's information, regardless of the probability of the IRS's audit coverage.
questions.explanationJa: CPAは顧客から得た情報を、検証せずに誠実に信頼して申告書を作成してよい。ただし、提供された情報が不正確・不完全・不整合に見える場合には無視することは許されず、職業的な知識と判断に基づいて合理的な質問を行い、疑問点を解消しなければならない。いわば「合理性テスト」であり、すべての情報を検証する義務はないが、自動的に受け入れてよいわけでもない。また、IRSの税務調査の実施率が低いことは、疑問点の調査を省略する理由にならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.4

questions.stem: A CPA prepares income tax returns for a client. After the client signs and mails the returns, the CPA discovers an error. According to Treasury Circular 230, the CPA is required to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Resign from the engagement if the client refuses to authorize filing an amended return.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prepare an amended return within 30 days of the discovery of the error.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Promptly advise the client of the error.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reimburse the client if the error was the CPA's fault and resulted in a penalty over $500.

questions.explanation:
When a tax practitioner (CPA) becomes aware of an incident of a client's noncompliance with revenue laws, or of an error or omission on a filing with the IRS (previously filed return), the CPA is required to:

Promptly advise the client of the error, and

Advise the client of the potential consequences of that error (accuracy-related penalty).

The rule ensures that the error will be brought to the client's attention in a timely manner and that the client will receive the proper information necessary to decide how to correct the error (file an amended return).

However, it's the client, not the CPA, who ultimately decides whether to correct the error, such as by filing an amended return. There is no time limit for correcting the error, but in addition to a penalty, the client is responsible for interest that will accrue on any unpaid tax due to the error.

("Resign from the engagement if the client refuses to authorize filing…") The CPA and client may disagree about how to correct the error. If it is significant enough, the CPA may choose to resign from additional work for the client. However, Cir 230 does not require this.

("Reimburse the client if the error was the CPA's fault and resulted in…") Although some CPAs may choose to reimburse a client for tax penalties caused by the CPA's error, Cir 230 does not require it.
questions.explanationJa: Circular 230の下では、税務実務家が顧客の法令違反や過去に提出された申告書の誤り・脱漏を知った場合、速やかに顧客にその誤りを伝え、その結果（正確性関連ペナルティなど）を助言しなければならない。誤りをどう是正するか（修正申告を行うか）を最終的に決めるのはCPAではなく顧客である。修正申告を30日以内に作成する義務、顧客が修正申告を拒んだ場合に辞任する義務、CPAの過失によるペナルティを補填する義務は、いずれもCircular 230には定められていない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.5

questions.stem: The disclosure of a tax return position will reduce or eliminate an accuracy-related penalty on the taxpayer in which of the following circumstances?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The position is frivolous.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The position is not properly substantiated.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The position concerns a tax shelter with substantial authority.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The position does not concern a tax shelter and has a reasonable basis.

questions.explanation:
The IRC imposes an accuracy-related penalty for misstatements in a tax return that create a tax underpayment. The penalty is 20% of the underpayment and is in addition to the tax. Sometimes, to minimize taxes, taxpayers may take positions in their tax returns that are based on disputed tax law. The IRS may assess an accuracy-related penalty for the understatement of tax relating to the disputed tax position.

Taxpayers can avoid the penalty in certain circumstances.

Tax positions based on substantial authority (40% chance of being sustained on the merits) will avoid the penalty. These tax positions do not have to be disclosed (substantiated) on the tax return

Tax positions that have a reasonable basis for the position (20% chance of being sustained on the merits) will also avoid the penalty, but only if they are adequately disclosed in the tax return

However, a taxpayer using a tax position based on a tax shelter will not avoid the penalty regardless of the type of tax position.

("The position is frivolous.") Frivolous tax positions (less than 20% chance of being sustained on the merits) are subject to the accuracy-related penalty in all circumstances.
questions.explanationJa: 正確性関連ペナルティは、申告書の誤りにより生じた過少納付額の20%を税額に上乗せして課される。実質的根拠（認容可能性おおむね40%）のあるポジションは開示しなくてもペナルティを免れるが、合理的根拠（おおむね20%）しかないポジションは、申告書で適切に開示した場合に限りペナルティを免れる。したがって、タックスシェルターに関係せず合理的根拠のあるポジションは、開示によってペナルティが軽減・免除される。一方、タックスシェルターに関するポジションは開示してもペナルティを免れず、根拠の乏しい（20%未満の）ポジションはどのような場合でもペナルティの対象となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.6

questions.stem: Pursuant to Treasury Department Circular No. 230, which of the following statements about the return of a client's records is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Copies of the client's records must be destroyed 3 years after the tax return was filed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The practitioner may retain copies of the client's records.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The existence of a dispute over fees generally relieves the practitioner of responsibility to return the client's records.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The practitioner does not need to return any client records that may be necessary to document a tax position that was disclosed on the tax return.

questions.explanation:
To properly maintain their client files, practitioners are allowed to retain copies of all tax records provided by their clients. This provision is especially important when a practitioner takes a position on a client's tax return that is based on disputed tax law. However, this allowance does not relieve the practitioner of the duty to return the client's tax records when asked to do so.

("Copies of the client's records must be destroyed 3 years after the ta…") Generally, practitioners are required to either retain copies of completed returns for 3 years or retain a list of clients for the prior 3 years. There is no requirement for a practitioner to destroy copies of a client's tax records after 3 years.

("The existence of a dispute over fees generally relieves the practitio…") If there is a fee dispute the practitioner may withhold some documents. However, a practitioner is required to return all of the client's records that are necessary for the client to comply with federal tax obligations (eg, receipts for meals and entertainment).
questions.explanationJa: 実務家は、顧客ファイルを適切に管理するため、顧客から提供された税務記録の写しを保持することが認められている。これは、係争中の税法解釈に基づくポジションを申告書で取った場合に特に重要である。ただし、写しを保持できるからといって、顧客から求められた記録の原本を返却する義務がなくなるわけではない。報酬をめぐる争いがあっても、顧客が連邦税の義務を果たすのに必要な記録は返却しなければならず、また3年経過後に記録の写しを廃棄する義務も存在しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.7

questions.stem: According to Treasury Circular 230, which of the following rules related to the prompt disposition of pending matters before the IRS applies to CPAs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Practitioners may request an extension of time of not more than five years related to the disposition of matters pending before the IRS to avoid any preparer penalties.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Practitioners will be held responsible for any of the client's interest and penalties related to the unreasonable delay of matters pending before the IRS.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Practitioners may not unreasonably delay the prompt disposition of matters pending before the IRS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Practitioners must ensure that matters are concluded within three years of the date of formal notification concerning any matters pending before the IRS.

questions.explanation:
CPAs may not unreasonably delay the prompt disposition of any matter before the IRS.

There is no mention of the time frame for how long pending matters can be extended or when they must be concluded ("Practitioners may request an extension of time of not more than five…" / "Practitioners must ensure that matters are concluded within three yea…"). Although a CPA may be disciplined under Circular 230 for unreasonably delaying a matter, Circular 230 does not impose interest and penalties on the client for the CPA's unreasonable delay
questions.explanationJa: Circular 230は、CPAがIRSに係属している案件の迅速な処理を不当に遅延させてはならないと定めている。係属案件をどれだけ延長できるか、あるいはいつまでに終結させなければならないかという具体的な期間は定められていない。CPAが不当に遅延させた場合はCircular 230に基づく懲戒の対象になり得るが、それによって顧客に生じた利息やペナルティをCPAが負担するという規定はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.8

questions.stem: Under the Internal Revenue Code, a CPA who was engaged in the business of preparing tax returns could incur a penalty for disclosing taxpayer information without the taxpayer's formal consent in which of the following circumstances?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The information was disclosed in the client's state and local tax returns that the CPA prepared.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The information was disclosed in the client's electronically filed tax return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The information was disclosed pursuant to an attorney's solicitation request.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The information was disclosed pursuant to a court order.

questions.explanation:
The IRS rules governing tax return preparers prohibit the CPA from knowingly or recklessly disclosing a taxpayer's information or using the information other than to prepare the tax return. The preparer is not permitted to reveal this information to third parties (an attorney's solicitation request) without the consent of the taxpayer except in limited circumstances. Because the CPA does not have the taxpayer's formal consent, the information may not be disclosed to an attorney's solicitation request (request for referrals).

("The information was disclosed in the client's state and local tax ret…" / "The information was disclosed in the client's electronically filed ta…") The CPA may disclose the information to prepare related tax returns (state, local) and electronically file the returns.

("The information was disclosed pursuant to a court order.") Exceptions to this rule include situations in which an authoritative body requires the CPA to disclose the information (subpoena, court order, peer review).
questions.explanationJa: IRSの規則は、税務申告書作成者が顧客の情報を故意または無謀に開示したり、申告書作成以外の目的に使用したりすることを禁じている。弁護士からの勧誘依頼（紹介の求め）に応じて情報を開示することは、顧客の正式な同意がない限り認められず、ペナルティの対象となる。一方、関連する州・地方税の申告書の作成や電子申告のための利用は認められている。また、裁判所命令や召喚状、ピアレビューなど権限ある機関から開示を求められた場合も例外として開示できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.9

questions.stem: According to Treasury Department Circular 230, under which of the following circumstances may a tax practitioner charge a contingent fee for services?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Preparing previous years' income tax returns that the taxpayer had failed to file on time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtaining a refund for the taxpayer by amending a previous year's income tax return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reviewing previous returns filed by a different tax practitioner to find an error on which to base a refund claim.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assisting the taxpayer to obtain a refund in connection with statutory penalties and interest charged by the IRS.

questions.explanation:
A tax practitioner is allowed to charge a contingent fee for services relating to:

An examination (audit) of or challenge to an original or amended return, or a claim for refund

A claim for credit or refund in connection with statutory interest or penalties assessed by the IRS

A judicial proceeding under the IRC (filing a private letter ruling)

Contingent fees are not allowed for filing an original return (even if it's late) ("Preparing previous years' income tax returns that the taxpayer had fa…"). The prohibition also applies to filing refund claims for tax matters that have not been challenged or examined by the IRS
questions.explanationJa: Circular 230の下で成功報酬が認められるのは、原申告書・修正申告書や還付請求に対するIRSの調査・異議に関するサービス、IRSが課した法定の利息やペナルティに関する還付・税額控除の請求、内国歳入法に基づく司法手続きに関するサービスである。したがって、IRSが課したペナルティと利息について還付を受けるための支援には成功報酬を請求できる。期限後であっても原申告書を作成する場合には成功報酬は認められず、IRSの調査や異議の対象となっていない事項について還付請求を行う場合（修正申告による還付、他の作成者の過去の申告書から誤りを探す場合）も同様に認められない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.10

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct concerning a penalty for a tax return preparer who understates a taxpayer's liability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No penalty is imposed if the understatement of tax liability is related to a tax shelter and was properly disclosed, and there was substantial authority for the position.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If there is a final judicial decision that there was no understatement of liability, the related tax preparer penalty paid earlier is not refundable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In general, the penalty does not apply unless the understatement of the tax liability is at least $10,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No penalty is imposed if it is shown that there is reasonable cause for the understatement and the tax return preparer acted in good faith.

questions.explanation:
A position is considered unreasonable when the preparer knew, or should have known, that the position lacks substantial authority. However, a preparer can take a position that lacks substantial authority and avoid the penalty if the position is disclosed and there is a reasonable basis for taking the position.

In addition, this penalty will not apply if there was reasonable cause for the understatement and the preparer acted in good faith (faulty tax software, reliance on incorrect advice from IRS). Willful or reckless conduct occurs when the preparer disregards an obvious, well-settled tax rule. There is no reasonable cause/good faith penalty waiver for willful or reckless conduct.

("No penalty is imposed if the understatement of tax liability is relat…") The understatement rules have a special provision for tax shelters. There is no penalty if the position is disclosed to the IRS and there is a more than likely (greater than 50%) chance of the position being upheld. Substantial authority (40% likelihood) for the position to be upheld is not enough to avoid the penalty.

("If there is a final judicial decision that there was no understatemen…") If a preparer pays an understatement penalty and it's later determined that there was no understatement, then the penalty will be refunded.

("In general, the penalty does not apply unless the understatement of t…") The penalty applies regardless of the amount of the understatement.
questions.explanationJa: 作成者は、実質的根拠を欠くことを知っていた、または知るべきであったポジションを取った場合に過少申告ペナルティを課されるが、合理的な理由があり、かつ誠実に行動したことを示せばペナルティは課されない（税務ソフトの不具合やIRSの誤った助言への依拠など）。ただし、明白な税法規定を故意・無謀に無視した場合にはこの免除はない。タックスシェルターについては、開示したうえで「more likely than not（50%超）」の可能性が必要であり、実質的根拠（40%）だけではペナルティを免れない。また、後に過少申告がなかったと判断されれば支払済みのペナルティは還付され、ペナルティは過少申告額の大小にかかわらず適用される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.11

questions.stem: Each of the following constitutes substantial authority for a taxpayer to take a tax position, except

choices.label: A
choices.text: A determination letter conclusion in which the taxpayer is named.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A technical advice memorandum conclusion in which the taxpayer is named.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An affirmative statement in a revenue agent's report with respect to a prior year of the taxpayer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A private letter ruling in which the taxpayer is named and that is inconsistent with a subsequently issued Treasury Regulation.

questions.explanation:
A taxpayer can rely on any IRS interpretation in which the IRS directly refers to that taxpayer and determines how the tax laws relate to the taxpayer's specific tax situation. If the IRS interpretation favors a position the taxpayer plans to take in its tax return, the interpretation represents substantial authority for that position. Examples of IRS interpretations include:

Determination letter--a formal ruling by the IRS on the qualification status of an employer's retirement plan ("A determination letter conclusion in which the taxpayer is named.")

Technical advice memorandum--guidance given by the IRS Office of Chief Counsel to an IRS official who needs specific rulings on a taxpayer's technical or procedural matters ("A technical advice memorandum conclusion in which the taxpayer is nam…")

Revenue agent's report--a report issued by an IRS examiner detailing the findings and conclusions of a tax audit ("An affirmative statement in a revenue agent's report with respect to…")

A private letter ruling (PLR) is a formal interpretation of how the IRS believes then current tax laws should be applied to a taxpayer's situation. The taxpayer can rely on this interpretation when taking a position in a tax return, and the IRS will be required to follow the PLR. However, if Treasury Regulations are subsequently issued that are inconsistent with the PLR, the PLR is no longer valid.
questions.explanationJa: IRSが特定の納税者を名指しして、その納税者の状況に税法をどう適用するかを判断した解釈は、その納税者にとって実質的根拠となる。たとえば、退職給付制度の適格性に関する決定通知書（determination letter）、IRS首席法律顧問室が出す技術的助言メモランダム（TAM）、税務調査の結論を記載した調査官報告書がこれに当たる。プライベート・レター・ルーリング（PLR）も本来は依拠できる解釈だが、その後にPLRと矛盾する財務省規則が公布されると効力を失う。したがって、後の財務省規則と矛盾するPLRは実質的根拠にならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.12

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a notice of deficiency from the IRS. If the tax underpayment is not the result of the taxpayer's mathematical or clerical error, how long does the taxpayer have to file a petition with the Tax Court for a redetermination of the deficiency?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the notice is addressed to a taxpayer outside of the United States, 120 days from the mailing date of the notice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sixty days from the mailing date of the notice if the notice is not addressed to a taxpayer outside of the United States.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the taxpayer has filed for bankruptcy under Chapter 11, 150 days from the mailing date of the notice.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ninety days from the mailing date of the notice if the notice is not addressed to a taxpayer outside of the United States.

questions.explanation:
After the IRS assesses a deficiency, it sends the taxpayer a 30-day letter explaining its reasoning along with a copy of the audit examination report. This gives the taxpayer 30 days to accept the proposed change, skip the appeal process, or request a conference with an appeals officer.

If the taxpayer disagrees with the appeal determination or does not respond to the 30-day letter, the IRS issues a notice of deficiency (90-day letter). The notice of deficiency gives a taxpayer with a United States address 90 days from the notice's mailing date to either pay the deficiency or file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court. A taxpayer with an address outside the United States has 150 days ("If the notice is addressed to a taxpayer outside of the United States…").

("Sixty days from the mailing date of the notice if the notice is not a…") A notice of deficiency gives United States residents 90 days (not 60 days) from the notice's mailing date to file a petition with the Tax Court.

("If the taxpayer has filed for bankruptcy under Chapter 11, 150 days f…") There are no special time limits for taxpayers who have filed for any type of bankruptcy.
questions.explanationJa: IRSは不足税額を査定すると、まず30日レターで理由と調査報告書を送り、納税者は30日以内に変更を受け入れるか、不服審査官との協議を求めることができる。納税者が不服審査の結論に同意しないか30日レターに応答しない場合、IRSは不足税額通知（90日レター）を発行する。米国内に住所がある納税者は、通知の郵送日から90日以内に不足税額を納付するか租税裁判所に申立てをしなければならない。米国外の住所の納税者は150日であり（120日ではない）、破産した納税者について特別な期間はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.13

questions.stem: Which of the following situations will not result in a tax preparer's penalty?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At a client's insistence, the preparer takes and properly discloses a tax position that does not meet the reasonable basis standard.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The preparer discloses a client's personally identifying information to outside parties to permit the electronic submission of the client's return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The preparer retains a copy of the client's prepared tax return for 2 years before shredding the return.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The preparer provides a preparer tax identification number but fails to sign a client's tax return.

questions.explanation:
Tax preparers generally are subject to a penalty for disclosing confidential information obtained through the preparation of a return. However, exceptions exist, including the provision of information to permit electronic preparation or submission of a return. This allows software companies to transmit tax returns to the IRS for tax preparers.

("At a client's insistence, the preparer takes and properly discloses a…") Tax preparers will not incur penalties for tax positions that meet the substantial authority standard or for positions that meet the reasonable basis standard and are disclosed. If a position does not meet the reasonable basis standard, a penalty may apply, even with disclosure.

("The preparer retains a copy of the client's prepared tax return for 2…") Preparers must retain copies of completed returns or a list of the names and taxpayer identification numbers for all returns prepared for 3 years. If a return was retained for only 2 years, a penalty may apply.

("The preparer provides a preparer tax identification number but fails…") To avoid a penalty, tax preparers must provide their preparer tax identification numbers and sign every return prepared.
questions.explanationJa: 税務申告書作成者は、申告書作成を通じて得た秘密情報を開示するとペナルティの対象となるのが原則だが、申告書の電子的な作成・提出を可能にするための情報提供は例外として認められている。このため、電子申告のために顧客の個人識別情報を外部に提供してもペナルティは課されない。一方、合理的根拠の基準を満たさないポジションは開示してもペナルティの対象となり得る。また、作成済み申告書の写し（または顧客名と納税者番号の一覧）は3年間保存しなければならず2年での廃棄はペナルティの対象となり、PTINを記載するだけでなく申告書への署名も必要である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.14

questions.stem: An unmarried taxpayer with income exclusively from wages filed their initial income tax return for the Year 8 calendar year. By December 31, Year 8, the taxpayer's employer had withheld $16,000 in federal income taxes and the taxpayer had made no estimated tax payments. On April 15, Year 9, the taxpayer timely filed an extension request to file their individual tax return and paid $300 of additional taxes. The taxpayer's Year 8 income tax liability was $16,500 when they timely filed their return on April 30, Year 9, and paid the remaining income tax liability balance. What amount would be subject to the penalty for the underpayment of estimated taxes?
questions.explanation:
To avoid underpayment penalties, a taxpayer must pay a safe harbor amount. This amount is the lesser of 100% of the prior year's tax liability (110% if the prior year's AGI is over $150,000) or 90% of the current year tax liability. There is no penalty if the balance due on the return is less than $1,000.

In this scenario, the taxpayer had a balance due of $200 ($16,500 tax liability − $16,000 withholding - $300). Because the balance due ($200) is less than $1,000, no penalty will apply
questions.explanationJa: 推定税額の過少納付ペナルティを避けるには、前年の税額の100%（前年のAGIが$150,000超なら110%）と当年の税額の90%のいずれか少ない額をセーフハーバーとして納付する必要があるが、申告時の納付不足額が$1,000未満であればペナルティは課されない。本問では、税額$16,500から源泉徴収額$16,000と延長申請時の追加納付$300を差し引いた納付不足額は$200（$16,500 − $16,000 − $300）である。この$200は$1,000未満なので、過少納付ペナルティの対象となる金額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.15

questions.stem: Under Treasury Circular 230, the IRS requires that certain records be returned to a client by the tax practitioner even though no payment for services has been received. Records of the client for this purpose do not include

choices.label: A
choices.text: Materials prepared by a client's actuary and provided to the practitioner with respect to tax preparation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A schedule prepared by the practitioner that provides mathematical details of a particular amount included in a client's tax return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Electronic materials provided to the practitioner that existed before the client retained the practitioner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Written records given to the practitioner at the beginning of the engagement.

questions.explanation:
A tax practitioner must return a client's records even if the fee is unpaid. Client records are defined as:

Material given to the tax preparer that existed prior to the tax preparer's current engagement with the client ("Electronic materials provided to the practitioner that existed before…" / "Written records given to the practitioner at the beginning of the eng…").

Items prepared by the client or a third party ("Materials prepared by a client's actuary and provided to the practiti…").

Anything prepared by the tax preparer, and previously provided to the client, that the client needs to file the current-year tax return (prior-year tax returns).

However, the tax practitioner may withhold all material prepared during the current engagement until the client pays the fee for their preparation. This includes current-year returns, claims for refund, schedules, tax work papers, affidavits, or appraisals.
questions.explanationJa: 税務実務家は、報酬が未払いであっても顧客の記録を返却しなければならない。返却対象となる顧客の記録には、今回の業務より前から存在し実務家に提供された資料（電子的なものや業務開始時に渡された書面を含む）、顧客自身や第三者（アクチュアリーなど）が作成した資料、実務家が作成して以前に顧客に渡し当年の申告に必要なもの（前年の申告書など）が含まれる。一方、今回の業務の中で実務家が作成した資料は、報酬が支払われるまで留保できる。したがって、申告書に記載した金額の計算明細として実務家が作成したスケジュールは、返却義務のある顧客の記録に含まれない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.16

questions.stem: When a taxpayer needs guidance with a specific tax issue related to a proposed transaction, the taxpayer can ask the IRS for

choices.label: A
choices.text: A revenue ruling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A private letter ruling.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An extension.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A technical advice memorandum.

questions.explanation:
Taxpayers can ask the IRS to interpret and apply tax laws to the taxpayer's specific tax situation. The tax situation usually involves a proposed complex transaction that lacks definitive tax treatment. The resulting IRS interpretation is called a private letter ruling (PLR). Once the PLR is issued, the taxpayer can proceed with the transaction knowing how it will be taxed. A PLR is binding on the IRS only with respect to the specific taxpayer who requested the PLR.

("A revenue ruling.") A revenue ruling is an official interpretation of how the IRS applies tax statutes and regulations. Revenue rulings are much broader in scope than PLRs. For example, a revenue ruling may hold that taxpayers can deduct certain automobile expenses if they follow prescribed record keeping rules.

("An extension.") An extension is a request from a taxpayer for additional time to file a tax return.

("A technical advice memorandum.") A technical advice memorandum (TAM) is guidance furnished by the Office of Chief Counsel to advise an IRS director in regards to technical or procedural questions that develop during a proceeding.
questions.explanationJa: 納税者は、自らの具体的な税務状況（通常は取扱いが明確でない複雑な取引の予定）にIRSが税法をどう解釈・適用するかを照会できる。これに対するIRSの解釈をプライベート・レター・ルーリング（PLR）といい、納税者は課税関係を把握したうえで取引を進められる。PLRは照会した納税者についてのみIRSを拘束する。レベニュー・ルーリングはより一般的なIRSの公式解釈であり、技術的助言メモランダム（TAM）は手続き中に生じた問題についてIRS内部の担当者に助言するもの、延長は申告期限の延長の申請であって、いずれも個別の予定取引についての照会手段ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.17

questions.stem: While preparing a tax return for a new client and reviewing the client's prior-year return, a CPA noticed an error made by the client's former tax preparer. According to Treasury Department Circular 230, which of the following is the CPA specifically required to do in this case?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contact the tax preparer who made the error and suggest that an amended return be prepared for the client.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inform the client of the error and insist that the return be amended.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inform the client of the error and advise of the consequences.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Advise the client to contact the tax preparer of the prior-year return.

questions.explanation:
CPA is required to:

Promptly advise the client of the error, and

Advise the client of the potential consequences of that error (accuracy penalty).

This rule ensures that the error will be brought to the client's attention in a timely manner and that the client will have the information needed to decide how to correct the error (file an amended return).

Cir 230 does not require the CPA to insist that the erroneous prior return be amended ("Inform the client of the error and insist that the return be amended."). Nor does it require the CPA to specifically advise the client to contact a prior tax preparer ("Advise the client to contact the tax preparer of the prior-year retur…"). From a practical standpoint, amending the prior return may be necessary to correct the error. However, the client must ultimately make the decision after being informed of the error's consequences.

("Contact the tax preparer who made the error and suggest that an amend…") Directly contacting the prior tax preparer for any reason without first receiving the client's permission is prohibited by confidentiality rules.
questions.explanationJa: Circular 230の下では、CPAは過去に提出された申告書の誤りに気づいた場合、速やかに顧客に誤りを伝え、その結果（正確性関連ペナルティなど）を助言しなければならない。これにより、顧客は誤りをどう是正するか（修正申告を行うか）を判断するための情報を得られる。実務上は修正申告が必要になることが多いが、最終的に判断するのは顧客であり、修正申告を強く求めることや前任の作成者に連絡するよう助言することまでは求められていない。また、顧客の許可なく前任の作成者に直接連絡することは守秘義務に反する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.18

questions.stem: Which of the following acts constitutes grounds for a tax preparer penalty?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The tax preparer had a medical emergency and failed to sign the taxpayer's return.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the taxpayer's suggestion, the tax preparer deducted the expenses of the taxpayer's personal domestic help as a business expense on the taxpayer's individual tax return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Without the taxpayer's consent, the tax preparer disclosed taxpayer income tax return information under an order from a state court.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tax preparer failed to disclose a tax position that had substantial authority.

questions.explanation:
The IRS may assess an accuracy-related penalty on the preparer for the understatement of tax relating to the disputed tax position.

The preparer can avoid the penalty in certain circumstances.

Tax positions based on substantial authority (40% chance of being sustained on the merits) will avoid the penalty and do not have to be disclosed (substantiated) on the tax return ("The tax preparer failed to disclose a tax position that had substanti…")

Tax positions that have a reasonable basis (20% chance of being sustained on the merits) will also avoid the penalty, but only if they are adequately disclosed in the tax return

However, the preparer will be subject to an understatement penalty for willfully or recklessly disregarding the tax rules (taking a business deduction for a personal expense).

("The tax preparer had a medical emergency and failed to sign the taxpa…") Failing, without reasonable cause, to sign a client's return results in a preparer penalty. A medical emergency is considered reasonable cause.

("Without the taxpayer's consent, the tax preparer disclosed taxpayer i…") Preparers generally are subject to a penalty for disclosing confidential information obtained through the preparation of a return. However, exceptions exist, including disclosing taxpayer income tax return information under an order from a state court.
questions.explanationJa: 家事使用人の費用のような個人的支出を事業経費として控除することは、税法の規定を故意または無謀に無視するものであり、顧客の提案によるものであっても作成者は過少申告ペナルティの対象となる。一方、実質的根拠（おおむね40%）のあるポジションは開示しなくてもペナルティを免れる。正当な理由なく申告書に署名しない場合はペナルティの対象となるが、医療上の緊急事態は正当な理由と認められる。また、州裁判所の命令に基づく申告情報の開示は、秘密情報の開示禁止の例外に当たる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.19

questions.stem: A CPA prepared a tax return that involved a tax shelter transaction that was disclosed on the return. In which of the following situations would a tax return preparer penalty not be applicable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There was substantial authority for the position.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is reasonable to believe that the position would more likely than not be upheld.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There was a reasonable possibility of success for the position.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There was a reasonable basis for the position.

questions.explanation:
Tax return preparer understatement penalties:
Probability of success: Significance of threshold
More likely than not > 50%: Understatement penalty applies for reportable transactions that do not meet this threshold
Substantial authority ≈ 40%: Understatement penalty applies for undisclosed tax positions that do not meet this threshold
Realistic possibility ≈ 33%: AICPA SSTSs* require members to meet this threshold as a minimum for undisclosed tax positions
Reasonable basis ≈ 20%: $5,000 penalty applies for positions that do not meet this threshold (ie, frivolous tax positions) Positions meeting this threshold must be disclosed to avoid penalty
*Statements on Standards for Tax Services (no longer tested on CPA exam).:

The disclosure requirements include all registered tax shelters and any special arrangement that changes reportable income by more than $10 million.

Tax preparers may be subject to penalties for failure to disclose such activities, even when there is no determination of an underpayment of taxes. Because of their aggressive nature, such activities also must meet the higher standard of "more likely than not" to succeed on their merits for the preparer to avoid penalty. "More likely than not" requires that the position have a greater than 50% likelihood of being sustained if challenged by the IRS.

("There was substantial authority for the position.") A position with substantial authority has an approximately 40% chance of success upon examination. Tax shelter transactions require a higher standard.

("There was a reasonable possibility of success for the position.") The term reasonable possibility is not used in the tax standards; the term is realistic possibility. A realistic possibility is a one-in-three chance of being successful.

("There was a reasonable basis for the position.") Reasonable basis means the position has roughly a 20% chance of success.
questions.explanationJa: 登録されたタックスシェルターや報告対象取引は、その積極的な性質から、作成者がペナルティを免れるには、開示したうえで「more likely than not」、つまりIRSに争われた場合に50%超の確率で認められる基準を満たす必要がある。実質的根拠（おおむね40%）や合理的根拠（おおむね20%）は、タックスシェルター取引には不十分である。また、「reasonable possibility」という用語は税務の基準には存在せず、使われているのは「realistic possibility（おおむね3分の1）」である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.20

questions.stem: Starr, CPA, prepared and signed Cox's current year federal income tax return. Cox informed Starr that Cox had paid doctors' bills of $20,000, although Cox actually had paid only $7,000 in doctors' bills during the year. Based on Cox's representations, Starr computed the medical expense deduction that resulted in an understatement of tax liability. Starr had no reason to doubt the accuracy of Cox's figures and Starr did not ask Cox to submit documentation of the expenses claimed. Cox orally assured Starr that sufficient evidence of the expenses existed. In connection with the preparation of Cox's return, Starr is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Liable to Cox for reimbursement of any interest on the underpayment of tax.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Liable to the IRS for negligently preparing the return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Not liable to the IRS for any penalty or interest.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Not liable to the IRS for any penalty but is liable to the IRS for interest on the underpayment of tax.

questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the CPA (Starr) had no reason to believe the information was incorrect. In addition, the taxpayer (Cox) assured Starr that proper documentation existed. Starr did everything required by the IRS when preparing a tax return that is partially based on a client's information. Therefore, Starr is not liable for any penalty or interest resulting from an understatement of tax due ("Liable to the IRS for negligently preparing the return." / "Not liable to the IRS for any penalty but is liable to the IRS for in…").

("Liable to Cox for reimbursement of any interest on the underpayment o…") IRS rules do not require a CPA to reimburse a client for interest the client had to pay due to a tax underpayment. However, some CPAs may choose to do so.
questions.explanationJa: Starrは、Coxの提示した数字を疑う理由がなく、Coxから十分な証拠が存在するとの保証も受けていた。顧客の情報に基づいて申告書を作成する場合にIRSが求めることをStarrはすべて行っているため、過少申告の結果についてIRSに対してペナルティも利息も負わない。したがって、過失による申告書作成を理由とする責任も、ペナルティはないが利息だけ負うという責任も生じない。また、IRSの規則は、過少納付により顧客が負担した利息をCPAが補填することを求めていない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.21

questions.stem:
An accuracy-related penalty applies to the portion of tax underpayment attributable to
I. Negligence or disregard of rules or regulations
II. Any substantial understatement of income tax
I | II

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
To make sure taxpayers file accurate returns and pay the proper amount of tax, the IRC imposes an accuracy-related penalty for misstatements in a tax return that create a tax underpayment. The penalty is equal to 20% of the underpayment and is in addition to the tax. It applies to any underpayment relating to:

Negligence or disregard of the tax rules or regulations ("No | Yes" / "No | No")

Any substantial understatement of income tax ("Yes | No")

Any substantial valuation misstatement for computing taxes (inflating an asset's basis to reduce the gain on sale)

Any substantial overstatement of pension liabilities

Any substantial estate or gift tax valuation understatement

Generally, a tax understatement is substantial if the underpayment exceeds the greater of either 10% of the tax that should be shown on the return, or $5,000.
questions.explanationJa: 正確性関連ペナルティは、申告書の誤りにより生じた過少納付額の20%を税額に上乗せして課される。対象となるのは、過失または規則・規定の無視による過少納付、所得税の重大な過少申告、税額計算上の重大な評価誤り、年金債務の重大な過大計上、遺産税・贈与税の重大な評価過少による過少納付である。したがって、過失・規則無視による過少納付と重大な過少申告の両方に適用される。なお、過少申告が重大と判断されるのは、一般に申告すべき税額の10%と$5,000のいずれか大きい額を超える場合である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.22

questions.stem: When preparing a client's Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, a CPA determined that there was documentation supporting only $12,000 of the $20,000 travel expenses claimed by the client. Which of the following courses of action taken by the CPA would be in compliance with Treasury Circular 230?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The CPA makes reasonable inquiries to obtain the needed documentation if the information as furnished appears to be incorrect or incomplete.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA deducts the $20,000 of expenses since there is a small likelihood that the IRS will audit the tax return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The CPA relies in good faith, without verification, upon information furnished by the client in deducting the expenses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The CPA deducts the $20,000 of expenses as long as the client agrees to disclose on the return that $8,000 of the expenses are undocumented.

questions.explanation:
CPA may, in good faith, rely on information provided by a taxpayer when preparing the client's tax return. The CPA has a duty to inquire about information that appears wrong or incomplete. Filing a return using incomplete information without making appropriate inquiries violates this duty. There are no exceptions, even for tax returns with a small likelihood of being audited ("The CPA deducts the $20,000 of expenses since there is a small likeli…").

Reliance is satisfied when the CPA believes the taxpayer's information is correct and is satisfied that the taxpayer has proper documentation (the client provided receipts) ("The CPA relies in good faith, without verification, upon information…"). The duty to inquire about incorrect and incomplete information is in place to encourage CPAs and tax preparers to comply with tax laws.

("The CPA deducts the $20,000 of expenses as long as the client agrees…") Filing the return and deducting the entire $20,000 in expenses and disclosing that $8,000 of the $20,000 are undocumented expenses is a willful understatement of a tax liability. Tax rules require that only documented travel expenses may be deducted. The CPA would most likely be subject to preparer penalties for knowingly deducting undocumented expenses on a tax return.
questions.explanationJa: CPAは顧客から提供された情報を誠実に信頼して申告書を作成してよいが、誤っている、または不完全と思われる情報については質問する義務がある。本問では$20,000の旅費のうち証拠があるのは$12,000だけなので、CPAは必要な書類を得るために合理的な質問をしなければならない。税務調査の可能性が低いことは、この義務の例外にならない。また、旅費は証拠のあるものしか控除できないため、$8,000が証拠のない経費だと開示したうえで$20,000全額を控除することは故意の過少申告に当たり、作成者ペナルティの対象となる可能性が高い。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.23

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the liability of a CPA for services performed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A CPA's work is not guaranteed to be accurate even though the CPA acted in a reasonably competent and professional manner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A CPA is negligent for exercising only that degree of care a reasonably competent CPA would exercise under the circumstances.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A CPA's liability for negligence extends only to the client and no further.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A CPA's liability for fraud extends only to the client and no further.

questions.explanation:
Accounting services are performed under a contract between the CPA and the client. For this reason, the most obvious liability facing a CPA is for common law negligence due to breach of contract. As one of the required elements to prove negligence, violation of at least one professional standard (GAAS) must be shown in a plaintiff's lawsuit against a CPA.

However, due professional care is not a guarantee of 100% accuracy. In fact, if mistakes occur, the CPA is not negligent as long as the CPA has exercised due professional care given the circumstances of the services being performed ("A CPA is negligent for exercising only that degree of care a reasonab…").

A CPA's liability for both negligence and fraud extends beyond the client to any party with privity ("A CPA's liability for negligence extends only to the client and no fu…" / "A CPA's liability for fraud extends only to the client and no further."). This means that parties suing a CPA must prove they are allowed to do so based on their legal relationship to the contractual agreement. The parties that typically have privity are the client, intended 3rd parties (creditors, investors), and foreseen 3rd parties
questions.explanationJa: 会計サービスはCPAと顧客の契約に基づいて提供されるため、CPAが負う最も典型的な責任は契約違反を理由とするコモンロー上の過失責任である。しかし、正当な職業上の注意は100%の正確性を保証するものではなく、状況に応じた正当な注意を払っていれば、誤りが生じても過失にはならない。したがって、合理的に有能で職業的な方法で業務を行ったとしても、CPAの業務の正確性は保証されない。なお、過失や詐欺についてのCPAの責任は顧客だけでなく、意図された第三者（債権者・投資家）や予見された第三者にも及ぶ。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.24

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best defense a CPA firm can assert in defense to a suit for common law fraud based on their unmodified opinion of materially false financial statements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lack of privity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lack of scienter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contributory negligence on the part of the client.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A disclaimer contained in the engagement letter.

questions.explanation:
Elements necessary to prove fraud or gross negligence (RIMS)

Reliance: Plaintiff justifiably relied on the financial information; no need for privity

Intent to deceive (two types):

Actual fraud: CPA knew the financial information was false (scienter)

Gross negligence: CPA recklessly disregarded the truth

Material misstatement: Financial information contained a material misstatement

Suffered loss: Plaintiff suffered a financial loss

Fraud is a common law principle of liability that can be asserted against a CPA. In addition to proving the other three elements of fraud (represented by RIMS), the party suing the CPA (plaintiff) must prove the CPA had the intent to deceive (scienter).

A CPA who proves that any element of RIMS did not happen can successfully defend a lawsuit based on common law fraud. As one defense, CPAs can argue that there was no intent to deceive when they mistakenly issued unmodified (clean) opinions.

("Lack of privity.") Privity is a legal relationship based on a mutual right or power to enforce a promise (contract). It is an element necessary to prove a CPA's negligence. However, privity is not one of the elements necessary to prove a CPA's fraud.

("Contributory negligence on the part of the client.") When proving fraud, there is no requirement that a plaintiff prove freedom from contributory negligence.

("A disclaimer contained in the engagement letter.") Generally, public policy prohibits anyone, including CPAs, from disclaiming fraud (ie, absolving themselves from it). Otherwise, people could avoid the consequences for unprofessional, harmful behavior.
questions.explanationJa: 詐欺（または重大な過失）を立証するには、原告は信頼（Reliance）、欺く意図（Intent to deceive）、重要な虚偽表示（Material misstatement）、損失の発生（Suffered loss）の4要素（RIMS）を立証しなければならない。欺く意図とは、CPAが財務情報の虚偽を知っていたこと（scienter）、または真実を無謀に無視したことをいう。CPAはいずれかの要素の不存在を示せば防御できるため、誤って無限定意見を出したが欺く意図はなかったという「scienterの欠如」が最善の抗弁となる。契約関係（privity）は過失の立証要素であって詐欺の要素ではなく、詐欺では顧客の寄与過失は問題にならず、公序の観点から詐欺についての免責条項も認められない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.25

questions.stem: To which of the following parties may a CPA partnership provide its working papers without being lawfully subpoenaed or without the client's consent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The IRS when the client is under investigation for tax fraud.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The SEC when the client is making a public offering.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A partner in the CPA's firm who is preparing the client's tax returns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Another CPA who is considering purchasing a partnership interest in the firm.

questions.explanation:
In this question, because the CPA partnership owns the working papers and all the partners are bound by the same rules of confidentiality, the papers can be shared with a partner in the firm without client approval. Nor is client approval required when sharing working papers in response to a court order, a valid legal or IRS administrative subpoena, or in connection with a peer review.

("The IRS when the client is under investigation for tax fraud." / "The SEC when the client is making a public offering.") Absent a subpoena, a CPA must not share working papers with the IRS or the SEC. The severity and magnitude of the circumstances are irrelevant.

("Another CPA who is considering purchasing a partnership interest in t…") Working papers may not be disclosed to an outside CPA without the client's consent. This restriction applies even if the disclosure is needed as part of a sale of the CPA's practice.
questions.explanationJa: 監査調書はCPA事務所が所有しており、事務所のパートナーは全員同じ守秘義務に服しているため、顧客の承認なしに事務所内のパートナーと共有できる。したがって、顧客の申告書を作成している事務所内のパートナーには、召喚状や顧客の同意がなくても調書を提供できる。裁判所命令、有効な召喚状やIRSの行政召喚状、ピアレビューの場合も顧客の承認は不要である。一方、召喚状がない限り、事情の深刻さにかかわらずIRSやSECに調書を提供してはならず、事務所の持分購入を検討している外部のCPAにも顧客の同意なしに開示できない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.26

questions.stem: A CPA's duty of due care to a client most likely will be breached when a CPA

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gives a client an oral instead of written report.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gives a client incorrect advice based on an honest error of judgment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fails to give tax advice that saves the client money.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fails to follow generally accepted auditing standards.

questions.explanation:
Examples of absence of due care from a CPA

Nondisclosure of information to the client (eg, I/C weakness)

Errors previously discovered but not corrected

Contract specifications not followed

Professional standards not followed:

State and federal law

GAAS, GAAP, etc.

Customs of the profession

the most obvious liability facing a CPA is for common law negligence due to breach of contract (failing to fulfill the terms of the agreement).

There are five elements to prove negligence. The party suing the CPA (plaintiff) must show, as one of the five, that the CPA failed to follow　due professional care. This is most often proved by showing that the CPA violated at least one professional standard (GAAS).

("Gives a client an oral instead of written report.") Oral reports are acceptable; however, most CPAs put their reports in writing to have a permanent record.

("Gives a client incorrect advice based on an honest error of judgment.") Due professional care is not a guarantee that a CPA's work is free from all errors. A CPA is not negligent for an honest error of judgment as long as the CPA exercises due professional care given the circumstances of the services being performed.

("Fails to give tax advice that saves the client money.") A CPA has no affirmative duty to give a client tax advice that saves the client money unless the CPA was hired to give tax-saving advice. Even in that situation, the CPA is not negligent for an honest error of not providing the tax-saving advice if the CPA exercised due professional care in performing the tax services.
questions.explanationJa: CPAに対する過失の主張では、原告は5つの要素の一つとしてCPAが正当な職業上の注意を怠ったことを示さなければならず、これは多くの場合、少なくとも一つの職業的基準（GAAS）に違反したことを示して立証される。したがって、一般に公正妥当と認められる監査基準に従わなかった場合、顧客に対する注意義務の違反となる可能性が最も高い。口頭での報告は認められており、正当な注意を払っていれば誠実な判断の誤りは過失にならない。また、節税助言を依頼されていない限り、顧客の税金を節約する助言をする積極的な義務もない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.27

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding disclosure of client working papers prepared by a CPA?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Working papers may not be transferred to an accountant outside the CPA's firm unless the client gives permission.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Working papers may not be turned over to a CPA quality review team without the client's permission.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Working papers may not be disclosed under a federal court subpoena without the client's permission.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Working papers may not be disclosed to any third parties without the client's permission.

questions.explanation:
In general, the CPA must maintain confidentiality and cannot provide the working papers or information obtained during engagements to other parties without the client's permission. However, there are exceptions, including:

Responding to a valid subpoena issued by a court or an IRS administrative subpoena ("Working papers may not be disclosed under a federal court subpoena wi…")

Providing the working papers as part of a quality control peer review ("Working papers may not be turned over to a CPA quality review team wi…")

Sharing the working papers with other members of the CPA's firm

A CPA does not need a client's permission to share working papers with other members, including CPAs, of the CPA's firm ("Working papers may not be disclosed to any third parties without the…"). Prohibiting CPAs in the same firm from sharing their working papers would make it difficult for them to work together. However, a CPA needs the client's permission to share working papers with other accountants outside the CPA's firm.
questions.explanationJa: CPAは原則として守秘義務を負い、顧客の許可なく監査調書や業務で得た情報を他者に提供できない。例外として、裁判所の有効な召喚状やIRSの行政召喚状への対応、品質管理のピアレビュー（品質レビューチーム）への提供、事務所内の他のメンバーとの共有が認められている。事務所内の共有まで禁じると協働が困難になるため、第三者への開示がすべて禁止されるわけではない。一方、事務所外の会計士に調書を渡すには顧客の許可が必要である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.28

questions.stem: Cable Corp. orally engaged Drake & Co., CPAs, to audit its financial statements. Cable's management informed Drake that it suspected the accounts receivable were materially overstated. Though the financial statements Drake audited included a materially overstated accounts receivable balance, Drake issued an unqualified opinion. Cable used the financial statements to obtain a loan to expand its operations. Cable defaulted on the loan and incurred a substantial loss. If Cable sues Drake for negligence in failing to discover the overstatement, Drake's best defense would be that Drake did not

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have privity of contract with Cable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sign an engagement letter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perform the audit recklessly or with an intent to deceive.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Violate generally accepted auditing standards in performing the audit.

questions.explanation:
[:No.29.png]

The party suing the accountant for common law negligence must prove all five CAMPS elements: causal relationship, absence of due care, material misstatement, privity, and a suffered loss.

In this scenario, the CPA firm (Drake & Co.) can attempt to prove any one of these elements is not present. If Drake proves that it used due professional care in performing the audit, it will not be liable for negligence. Drake can argue that it properly followed GAAS in performing the accounts receivable stage of the audit and therefore it is not negligent in failing to discover the overstatement.

("Have privity of contract with Cable.") Cable Corp. is Drake's client and therefore has privity.

("Sign an engagement letter.") There is no requirement under the statute of frauds that this contract (engagement letter) must be signed to be enforceable. Drake performed the services; therefore, it would be difficult to argue that there was no contract.

("Perform the audit recklessly or with an intent to deceive.") A CPA that performed accounting services recklessly or with an intent to deceive would be subject to charges of fraud or gross negligence, not common law negligence.
questions.explanationJa: コモンロー上の過失を理由に会計士を訴える原告は、因果関係、正当な注意の欠如、重要な虚偽表示、契約関係（privity）、損失の発生の5要素（CAMPS）をすべて立証しなければならない。Drakeはこのうちいずれかの要素の不存在を示せば責任を免れるため、GAASに従って売掛金の監査を行い正当な注意を払ったことを示すのが最善の抗弁となる。Cableは顧客なのでprivityは存在し、監査契約は書面を要する契約ではないため契約書に署名していないことも抗弁にならない。無謀に、または欺く意図をもって監査したかどうかは詐欺や重大な過失の問題であり、通常の過失の抗弁にはならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.29

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes whether a CPA has met the required standard of care in conducting an audit of a client's financial statements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The client's expectations with regard to the accuracy of audited financial statements.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The accuracy of the financial statements and whether the statements conform to generally accepted accounting principles.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whether the CPA conducted the audit with the same skill and care expected of an ordinarily prudent CPA under the circumstances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether the audit was conducted to investigate and discover all acts of fraud.

questions.explanation:
Due professional care means that the CPA used the same skill and care that an ordinarily prudent CPA would use in performing services under the same set of circumstances (audit).

("The client's expectations with regard to the accuracy of audited fina…") Due professional care is defined by industry and professional standards, not by the client's expectations.

("The accuracy of the financial statements and whether the statements c…") CPAs apply GAAS to determine reasonable assurance that financial statements conform to GAAP. If there are inaccuracies, the CPA is not negligent as long as the CPA exercises due professional care.

("Whether the audit was conducted to investigate and discover all acts…") During an audit, a CPA works to identify material misstatements due to fraud. Discovering all instances of fraud is impossible, and the due professional care standard does not require it.
questions.explanationJa: 正当な職業上の注意とは、同じ状況の下で通常の慎重なCPAが用いるのと同じ技能と注意を用いることをいう。したがって、監査で要求される注意基準を満たしたかどうかは、CPAがこの水準の技能と注意をもって監査を行ったかどうかで判断される。この基準は顧客の期待ではなく業界・職業上の基準で定まる。また、財務諸表に不正確な点があってもCPAが正当な注意を払っていれば過失にはならず、監査ですべての不正を発見することは不可能であり求められてもいない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.30

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding a CPA's working papers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Working papers need not be disclosed under a federal court subpoena.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Working papers must be disclosed under an IRS administrative subpoena.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Working papers must be disclosed to another accountant purchasing the CPA's practice.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Working papers need not be disclosed to a state CPA society quality review team.

questions.explanation:
CPA must maintain confidentiality and must obtain the client's permission before providing third parties with the working papers or information obtained during an engagement.

The exceptions to confidentiality include:

Responding to a valid subpoena issued by a court or an IRS administrative subpoena ("Working papers need not be disclosed under a federal court subpoena.")

Providing the working papers as part of a quality control peer review ("Working papers need not be disclosed to a state CPA society quality r…")

Sharing the working papers with other members of the CPA's firm.

Therefore, a CPA must provide client information, including working papers, when asked to do so under a valid subpoena issued by the IRS. Client permission is not needed.

("Working papers must be disclosed to another accountant purchasing the…") Acquiring a CPA practice does not automatically authorize the purchaser to access client information. The client's permission is required before the selling CPA can share the working papers with the purchaser.
questions.explanationJa: CPAは守秘義務を負い、監査調書や業務で得た情報を第三者に提供するには原則として顧客の許可が必要である。例外として、裁判所の有効な召喚状やIRSの行政召喚状への対応、品質管理のピアレビューへの提供、事務所内のメンバーとの共有が認められている。したがって、IRSの行政召喚状があれば、顧客の許可がなくても調書を開示しなければならない。連邦裁判所の召喚状や州CPA協会の品質レビューチームに対しても開示が必要であり、一方で事務所を買い取る会計士への開示には顧客の許可が必要である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.31

questions.stem: A company engaged a CPA to perform an audit of the company's financial statements for Year 2 in order to apply for a bank loan. After the bank made the loan, it was discovered that the company's assets had been materially overstated. The overstatement was not discovered as part of the CPA's audit procedures. If the company defaulted on the loan and the case occurred in a jurisdiction that follows the Restatement rule, then the CPA could have liability to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bank, but not the company.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company, but not the bank.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neither the bank nor the company.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both the bank and the company.

questions.explanation:
Here, all the elements necessary to prove negligence (CAMPS) are met for the client. In addition, almost all of them are met for the bank. The biggest obstacle for the bank is proving that it has privity to the contract.

In the majority of states (those that follow the Restatement of Torts), privity exists for

Client: The party that actually hired the CPA to perform the audit

Foreseen party: Anyone the CPA actually knew was an intended third party

Foreseeable party: Anyone the CPA could reasonably foresee as a third party. However, a minority of states don't allow privity for a foreseeable party.

Here, the CPA knew that the audit was being performed so that the client could secure a bank loan. Therefore, it's reasonable to assume that the CPA knew the financial statements would be given to a bank as part of the client's loan application, so the bank is a foreseeable third party. As a result, the client and the bank both have privity to the auditing contract, and the CPA could have negligence liability to both entities.
questions.explanationJa: 顧客である会社については、過失の立証要素（CAMPS）がすべて満たされている。銀行についてはprivityの立証が主な障害となるが、Restatement（不法行為法リステイトメント）に従う多数の州では、顧客に加えて、CPAが情報利用者として現に知っていた第三者にもprivityが認められる。本問のCPAは、監査が銀行融資を申し込むために行われることを知っていたので、財務諸表が融資申請の一部として銀行に渡されることも知っていたと考えられる。したがって、会社と銀行の両方がprivityを有し、CPAは両者に対して過失責任を負う可能性がある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.32

questions.stem: A CPA will be liable to a tax client for damages resulting from all of the following actions except

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failing to file a client's return in a timely manner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failing to advise a client of certain tax elections.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failing to sign a client's filing extension.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failing to determine if the client's return as married filing separately would result in lower taxes for married taxpayers.

questions.explanation:
In tax return preparation, due professional care means that a client's return is prepared so that the client will be liable for the minimum amount of taxes it is legally required to pay. This includes:

Timely filing the return to avoid late filing penalties ("Failing to file a client's return in a timely manner.")

Advising the client of all available tax elections (eg, Section 179 expense deduction) ("Failing to advise a client of certain tax elections.")

Evaluating and considering all options that will lower the tax liability for the client (filing joint versus married filing separate) ("Failing to determine if the client's return as married filing separat…")

A CPA who fails to exercise due professional care when preparing a client's tax return will be liable to that client for any damages resulting from negligently preparing the return. Generally, damages will equal the difference between the taxes the client paid and the taxes the client should have paid had the return been prepared properly. Damages may also include any penalties the client paid due to the CPA's negligence.

The CPA is required to sign the tax return. However, the CPA is not required to sign the extension. There is no penalty imposed for failing to sign a client's extension; therefore, it will not result in any damages.
questions.explanationJa: 税務申告書の作成における正当な職業上の注意とは、顧客が法律上納付すべき最小限の税額だけを負担するよう申告書を作成することをいう。これには、延滞ペナルティを避けるための期限内の申告、利用可能な税務上の選択（Section 179の即時償却など）の助言、夫婦合算申告と個別申告の比較など税額を下げる方法の検討が含まれ、これを怠ったCPAは顧客に生じた損害（本来納付すべきだった税額との差額やペナルティ）について責任を負う。一方、CPAは申告書には署名しなければならないが、延長申請書への署名は求められていない。延長申請書に署名しなくてもペナルティは生じないため、損害は発生しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.33

questions.stem: When performing an audit, a CPA will most likely be considered negligent when the CPA fails to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Detect all of a client's fraudulent activities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Include a negligence disclaimer in the client engagement letter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Warn a client of known internal control weaknesses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Warn a client's customers of embezzlement by the client's employees.

questions.explanation:
Due professional care means that the CPA used the same skill and care that an ordinarily prudent CPA would use in performing services under the same set of circumstances (audit). An auditor is required to communicate with the client regarding all identified significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in internal control (I/C). Therefore, failure to inform an audit client of known I/C weaknesses is considered negligence.

("Detect all of a client's fraudulent activities.") During an audit, a CPA works to identify material misstatements due to fraud. However, discovering all fraudulent acts is impossible, and exercising due professional care does not require it.

("Include a negligence disclaimer in the client engagement letter.") Generally, public policy prohibits anyone, including a CPA, from disclaiming negligence. Otherwise people would be able to avoid the consequences for unprofessional, harmful behavior.

("Warn a client's customers of embezzlement by the client's employees.") An auditor who discovers embezzlement must report it to the client's appropriate level of management (audit committee, controller, CFO). Informing a client's customers would violate the CPA's duty of confidentiality to the client.
questions.explanationJa: 正当な職業上の注意とは、同じ状況の下で通常の慎重なCPAが用いるのと同じ技能と注意を用いることをいう。監査人は、識別した内部統制の重要な不備および重大な欠陥をすべて顧客に伝えなければならないため、把握している内部統制の欠陥を顧客に知らせないことは過失とみなされる。監査ですべての不正を発見することは不可能であり求められておらず、公序の観点から過失についての免責条項を契約書に入れることも認められない。また、従業員の横領を発見した場合は顧客の適切な経営者層（監査委員会など）に報告すべきであり、顧客の取引先に知らせることは守秘義務に反する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.34

questions.stem: Thorp, CPA, was engaged to audit Ivor Co.'s financial statements. During the audit, Thorp discovered that Ivor's inventory contained stolen goods. Ivor was indicted and Thorp was subpoenaed to testify at the criminal trial. Ivor claimed accountant-client privilege to prevent Thorp from testifying. Which of the following statements is correct regarding Ivor's claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ivor can claim an accountant-client privilege only in states that have enacted a statute creating such a privilege.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ivor can claim an accountant-client privilege only in federal courts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The accountant-client privilege can be claimed only in civil suits.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The accountant-client privilege can be claimed only to limit testimony to audit subject matter.

questions.explanation:
In most states communications between CPAs and clients lack the legal privilege that protects the privacy of attorney-client communications. However, a small number of states have enacted privilege statutes for CPAs. In those states, the privilege can allow a subpoenaed CPA to refuse to testify in state court. The privilege applies in both criminal and civil cases ("The accountant-client privilege can be claimed only in civil suits."). In addition, it applies to all confidential information the CPA possesses about the client and therefore is not limited to audit-related subjects ("The accountant-client privilege can be claimed only to limit testimon…").

("Ivor can claim an accountant-client privilege only in federal courts.") The federal government recognizes working papers developed in connection with the preparation of a tax return to be privileged in noncriminal tax disputes with the IRS. That privilege would not apply to this scenario, even if the case were in federal court.
questions.explanationJa: 多くの州では、CPAと顧客の間のやり取りには、弁護士と依頼人の間のような法的な秘匿特権が認められていない。ただし、少数の州はCPAについて秘匿特権を定める法律を制定しており、その州では召喚されたCPAが州裁判所での証言を拒否できる場合がある。したがって、Ivorが会計士・顧客間の秘匿特権を主張できるのは、そうした法律を制定した州に限られる。この特権は刑事・民事の双方に適用され、監査に関する事項に限らずCPAが保有する顧客の秘密情報全般に及ぶ。連邦では、税務申告書作成に関連する調書について刑事事件以外のIRSとの税務紛争で特権が認められているにすぎず、本問の刑事裁判には適用されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.35

questions.stem: Which of the following is not under the jurisdiction of the Internal Revenue Service?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gift tax

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sales tax

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excise tax

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estate tax

questions.explanation:
Under the U.S. Constitution, the federal government is authorized to levy and collect taxes. The Department of the Treasury is the federal entity that administers this duty. The IRS is a bureau within the Treasury Department that is responsible for enforcing all revenue laws. The IRS's jurisdiction covers all federal taxes, including income taxes, excise taxes, payroll taxes, and gift and estate taxes ("Gift tax" / "Estate tax").

Excise taxes are applied to a specific type of good or service such as gambling services or motor fuel. Excise taxes exist at the federal, state, and local level. Excise taxes at the federal level fall under the jurisdiction of the IRS ("Excise tax").

Sales taxes generally apply to a broad range of goods and services and are typically calculated as a percentage of the total purchase. There are no laws allowing the federal government (via the IRS) to collect a sales tax. These taxes are collected at the state and local level and fall under the separate jurisdiction of each state and local government that has them.
questions.explanationJa: IRSは財務省の一部局として、所得税、物品税（excise tax）、給与税、贈与税・遺産税など、すべての連邦税を管轄している。物品税は賭博サービスや自動車燃料など特定の財・サービスに課される税で、連邦レベルのものはIRSの管轄に属する。一方、売上税（sales tax）は幅広い財・サービスに購入額の一定割合で課される税だが、連邦政府がこれを徴収することを認める法律は存在しない。売上税は州や地方で徴収され、それぞれの州・地方政府の管轄に属するため、IRSの管轄外である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.36

questions.stem:
To which of the following parties will a CPA be liable if the CPA fraudulently issues an unqualified opinion on a corporation's materially misstated financial statements?
Corporate shareholders | Corporate bondholders

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
Fraud is a common law principle of liability that can be asserted against a CPA by any party who used the financial information (shareholders and bondholders). Fraud refers to the intent to deceive and takes two basic forms:

Actual fraud: The CPA makes statements (the audit opinion) knowing they are false. For example, an auditor performs an audit, finds material misstatements in the financial statements, and issues an unqualified (clean) opinion anyway.

Gross negligence (constructive fraud): The CPA makes false statements with a reckless disregard for the truth, not knowing if the statements are true or false. This usually occurs when the CPA recklessly departs from the standard of due care while performing an engagement. For example, an auditor issues an unqualified opinion on unaudited financial statements that, had the CPA audited them, would have received an adverse opinion.

In ordinary negligence, only the foreseen users of the financial information can sue (ie, client and intended/foreseen 3rd parties). For fraud, any party who used the financial information can sue whether or not these users were foreseen.
