questions.explanationJa: 詐欺は、財務情報を利用したあらゆる者がCPAに対して主張できるコモンロー上の責任原理である。詐欺には、意見が虚偽であると知りながら表明する現実の詐欺と、真実を無謀に無視して虚偽の表明をする重大な過失（擬制詐欺）がある。通常の過失では、顧客と意図された・予見された第三者しか訴えることができないが、詐欺の場合は、予見されていたかどうかにかかわらず財務情報を利用した者は誰でも訴えることができる。したがって、CPAは株主と社債権者の双方に対して責任を負う。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.37

questions.stem: Phillips, CPA, was engaged by Veda, Inc. to audit Veda's financial statements. Phillips was told that the financial statements and the audit report were to be shown to Ryan, a potential investor. As a result of the audit, Phillips issued an audit report containing an unqualified opinion on Veda's financial statements. Ryan, after seeing the financial statements and audit report, made a substantial investment in Veda shares. Although Phillips exercised reasonable care in performing the audit, inaccuracies in the financial statements were later discovered, causing Veda share prices to fall. Ryan claimed that had Ryan known of the inaccuracies, Ryan would not have purchased the shares. Will Ryan succeed in a suit against Phillips for negligence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, because Ryan is a third-party beneficiary of the contractual relationship between Veda and Phillips.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, because Ryan relied on Phillips' unqualified opinion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, because Phillips owed no duty to Ryan.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because Phillips exercised reasonable care in performing the audit.

questions.explanation:
[:No.38.png]

A plaintiff suing for negligence must prove each of five elements (ie, CAMPS) to be successful in a negligence lawsuit. All five elements are discussed in the question but only four are satisfied.

Causal relationship? Yes, because Ryan suffered harm by relying on Phillip's work (audited financial statements) when deciding to purchase the Veda shares ("Yes, because Ryan relied on Phillips' unqualified opinion.").

Absence of reasonable care? No, because the facts state that reasonable care was exercised. Therefore, it is assumed Phillips followed GAAS and all other professional standards while performing the audit.

Material misstatement? Yes, because the financial statements contained inaccuracies significant enough to cause the Veda shares to drop in value.

Privity? Yes, because Phillips was explicitly told that Ryan was to be given the financial statements and audit report to make an investment decision ("Yes, because Ryan is a third-party beneficiary of the contractual rel…"). As a result, Phillips had a duty to Veda and Ryan ("No, because Phillips owed no duty to Ryan.").

Suffered loss? Yes, because Ryan's shares lost value when the Veda share price dropped due to the discovery of the inaccuracies.

Since Phillips used reasonable care, all five elements of proof are not met. Therefore, Ryan will not succeed in a lawsuit against Phillips.
questions.explanationJa: 過失訴訟で勝訴するには、原告は因果関係、正当な注意の欠如、重要な虚偽表示、契約関係（privity）、損失の発生の5要素（CAMPS）をすべて立証しなければならない。Ryanは監査済み財務諸表に依拠して株式を購入し損失を被っており、Phillipsは財務諸表がRyanに示されることを明示的に知らされていたのでRyanに対する義務（privity）もある。しかし、問題文ではPhillipsが監査で合理的な注意を払ったとされているため、正当な注意の欠如という要素が満たされない。5要素がそろわない以上、Ryanの過失訴訟は認められない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.38

questions.stem: A company engaged a CPA to perform the annual audit of its financial statements. The audit failed to reveal an embezzlement scheme by one of the employees. Which of the following statements best describes the CPA's potential liability for this failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The CPA's adherence to generally accepted auditing standards (GAAS) may prevent liability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA will not be liable if care and skill of an ordinarily reasonable person was exercised.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The CPA may be liable for punitive damages if due care was not exercised.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The CPA is liable for any embezzlement losses that occurred before the scheme should have been detected.

questions.explanation:
Due professional care means that the CPA used the same skill and care that an ordinarily prudent CPA would use in performing services under the same set of circumstances (audit). In common law negligence cases, professionals such as CPAs and doctors are held to higher standards (prudence) than an ordinarily reasonable person ("The CPA will not be liable if care and skill of an ordinarily reasona…").

("The CPA may be liable for punitive damages if due care was not exerci…") Punitive damages are generally not awarded in professional negligence lawsuits because this action would go beyond restoring injured parties to the economic position they were in before the negligence. Punitive damages are awarded in lawsuits involving a tort (bodily injury).

("The CPA is liable for any embezzlement losses that occurred before th…") The CPA may be liable for damages due to embezzlement losses that occurred after the audit. However, damages would not include losses that occurred before the audit, when the CPA could not have yet detected the scheme.
questions.explanationJa: 正当な職業上の注意とは、同じ状況の下で通常の慎重なCPAが用いるのと同じ技能と注意を用いることをいい、これは一般に公正妥当と認められる監査基準（GAAS）への準拠によって示される。したがって、監査で従業員の横領を発見できなくても、GAASに準拠していれば責任を免れる可能性がある。コモンロー上の過失では、CPAは通常の合理的な人より高い（慎重な専門家としての）水準を求められるため、通常人の注意を払ったというだけでは足りない。また、職業上の過失訴訟では一般に懲罰的損害賠償は認められず、CPAがまだ発見できなかった監査前の横領損失までは損害に含まれない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.39

questions.stem: An accounting firm was hired by a company to perform an audit. The company needed the audit report in order to obtain a loan from a bank. The bank lent $500,000 to the company based on the auditor's report. Fifteen months later, the company declared bankruptcy and was unable to repay the loan. The bank discovered that the accounting firm failed to discover a material overstatement of assets of the company. Which of the following statements is correct regarding a suit by the bank against the accounting firm? The bank

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cannot sue the accounting firm because of the statute of limitations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Can sue the accounting firm for the loss of the loan because of negligence.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cannot sue the accounting firm because there was no privity of contact.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Can sue the accounting firm for the loss of the loan because of the rule of privilege.

questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the audit was performed so the company could obtain a loan. This makes the bank an intended third party with privity to the audit services contract ("Cannot sue the accounting firm because there was no privity of contac…"). The other four elements needed to prove negligence are also present. Therefore, the bank can sue the accounting firm for the loss of the loan because of the firm's negligence.

("Cannot sue the accounting firm because of the statute of limitations.") A statute of limitations (SOL) is a legal rule that prevents a party from filing a lawsuit after a certain period has passed. The SOL period is set by state law in cases filed in state courts. For a breach-of-contract claim, the SOL period generally ranges from four to six years, depending on the state.

("Can sue the accounting firm for the loss of the loan because of the r…") Accountants are subject to the confidentiality requirements of the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct. However, there is no provision for an accountant-client privilege like those available to attorneys or physicians. In addition, such a privilege would not determine whether the bank in this scenario could sue the accounting firm.
questions.explanationJa: 本問の監査は、会社が銀行から融資を受けるために行われたものであるため、銀行は監査契約についてprivityを有する意図された第三者に当たる。過失の立証に必要な他の4つの要素（因果関係、正当な注意の欠如、重要な虚偽表示、損失の発生）も存在する。したがって、銀行は会計事務所の過失を理由に融資の損失について訴えることができる。契約違反に関する出訴期限は州により一般に4〜6年であり、15か月後の提訴を妨げない。また、会計士には弁護士や医師のような顧客との秘匿特権はなく、仮にあっても銀行が訴えられるかどうかを決めるものではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.40

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of elements must a client prove to hold an accountant liable for common law fraud?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Material misrepresentation and breach of contract.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Freedom from contributory negligence and loss.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scienter and justifiable reliance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intent to deceive and privity.

questions.explanation:
[:No.41.png]

Scienter and justifiable reliance are two of the four elements necessary to prove fraud (RIMS). The other two are that the CPA must have made a material misstatement and that the plaintiff must have suffered a loss.

The term "scienter," as used in the context of financial fraud, refers to the state of mind of the person who made the false statements. Scienter has two components:

The person knew the statements were false or was so reckless in verifying the statements that the person should have known they were false, and

The person made the false statements with the intent to deceive.

To prove justifiable reliance, clients need only prove they used the financial information in a substantive way (loan application).

("Material misrepresentation and breach of contract." / "Intent to deceive and privity.") Breach of contract is asserted only by someone who is in privity to the contract. A person is in privity if that person is either a party to the contract with the CPA (the client) or a known/foreseeable third party. Neither one is a necessary element to prove fraud.

("Freedom from contributory negligence and loss.") There is no requirement that the plaintiff prove freedom from contributory negligence. However, the plaintiff will have to refute it if the CPA asserts contributory negligence as a defense.
questions.explanationJa: 詐欺を立証するには、信頼（Reliance）、欺く意図すなわちscienter（Intent to deceive）、重要な虚偽表示（Material misstatement）、損失の発生（Suffered loss）の4要素（RIMS）が必要であり、scienterと正当な信頼はそのうちの2つである。scienterとは、陳述が虚偽であると知っていた（または知るべきであったほど無謀であった）うえで、欺く意図をもって虚偽の陳述をしたという心理状態をいう。正当な信頼は、顧客が融資申請などで財務情報を実質的に利用したことを示せば足りる。契約違反やprivityは詐欺の立証要素ではなく、原告が寄与過失のないことを立証する必要もない（CPAが抗弁として主張した場合に反論すればよい）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.41

questions.stem: In a common law action against an accountant, lack of privity is a viable defense if the plaintiff

choices.label: A
choices.text: Is the client's creditor who sues the accountant for negligence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Can prove the presence of gross negligence that amounts to a reckless disregard for the truth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Is the accountant's client.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bases the action upon fraud.

questions.explanation:
Privity is one of the five required elements to prove when suing an accountant for common law negligence. The accountant's client, as a party to the contract, always has privity ("Is the accountant's client.").

Other parties, such as intended third parties and foreseen parties, may also be affected by the accountant's negligence. Everyone else lacks privity because they are not directly affected by the accounting services. As a viable defense against a client's creditor who sues a CPA for negligence, the CPA can argue that the creditor was not an intended third party or a foreseen party and therefore lacks privity.

However, privity is not an element necessary to prove an accountant's fraud or gross negligence because fraud and gross negligence are considered egregious departures from professional standards ("Can prove the presence of gross negligence that amounts to a reckless…" / "Bases the action upon fraud."). As a matter of public policy, any party who used such financial information and suffered a loss may sue the accountant for fraud or gross negligence.

Note:
Privity is one of the five required elements (CAMPS) to prove when suing an accountant for common law negligence. It is not necessary to prove a CPA's liability for gross negligence or fraud. As a viable defense against a nonclient who sues a CPA for negligence, the CPA can argue that the nonclient was not an intended third party or a foreseen party and therefore lacks privity.
questions.explanationJa: privityは、会計士をコモンロー上の過失で訴える際に立証が必要な5要素の一つである。顧客は契約当事者なので常にprivityを有し、意図された第三者や予見された第三者もprivityを有し得るが、それ以外の者はprivityを欠く。したがって、顧客の債権者が過失を理由に訴えてきた場合、会計士はその債権者が意図された第三者でも予見された第三者でもないと主張して、privityの欠如を抗弁にできる。一方、詐欺や真実を無謀に無視する重大な過失はprivityを立証要素としないため、これらを根拠とする訴えに対してはprivityの欠如は抗弁にならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Ethics & Responsibilities in Tax Practice Q.42

questions.stem: According to the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, which of the following factors should a CPA consider in choosing whether to provide oral or written advice to a client?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whether the client will seek a second opinion

choices.label: B
choices.text: The tax sophistication of the client

choices.label: C
choices.text: The likelihood that current tax litigation will impact the advice

choices.label: D
choices.text: The client's business acumen

questions.explanation:
Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, a CPA uses professional judgment in deciding whether tax advice should be given orally or in writing. The factors to consider include the importance of the transaction and the amounts involved, the specific or general nature of the client's inquiry, the time available to develop and submit the advice, the technical complexity involved, the existence of authorities and precedents, and the tax sophistication of the client, among other factors. The tax sophistication of the client is one of these listed factors.

Whether the client will seek a second opinion is not a factor in choosing the form of the advice.
The likelihood that current tax litigation will affect the advice is not a listed factor for choosing between oral and written advice.
The client's business acumen is not the same as tax sophistication; general business skill does not indicate whether the client can understand and apply tax advice given orally.
questions.explanationJa:
AICPA の税務業務基準（SSTS）では、助言を口頭で行うか書面で行うかは職業的判断による。考慮要素は、取引の重要性と金額、照会の具体性、助言の作成に使える時間、技術的な複雑さ、先例・権威の有無、依頼人の税務に関する知識（tax sophistication）などで、依頼人の税務知識はその一つである。
依頼人がセカンドオピニオンを求めるかどうか、係争中の税務訴訟が助言に影響する可能性は、形式を選ぶ考慮要素に挙げられていない。依頼人のビジネスの才覚は税務知識とは別物で、口頭の助言を理解して使えるかの判断材料にはならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.2 (AICPA No. 9842)

questions.stem: Louis, the volunteer treasurer of a nonprofit organization and a member of its board of directors, compiles the data and fills out its annual Form 990, Return of Organization Exempt From Income Tax. Under the Internal Revenue Code, Louis is not considered a tax return preparer because

choices.label: A
choices.text: He is a member of the board of directors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The return does not contain a claim for a tax refund.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He is not compensated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Returns for nonprofit organizations are exempt from the preparer rules.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §7701(a)(36) and Treas. Reg. §301.7701-15, a tax return preparer is a person who prepares, or employs others to prepare, a return or claim for refund FOR COMPENSATION. Louis prepares the organization's Form 990 as an unpaid volunteer, so he is not a tax return preparer, and the preparer penalty and signature rules do not apply to him.

Being a member of the board of directors is not what removes Louis from the definition; compensation is the deciding factor, and a paid preparer could be a board member as well.
Whether the return claims a refund is irrelevant, because the definition covers both returns of tax and claims for refund.
Returns of nonprofit organizations are not exempt from the preparer rules; a person who prepares Form 990 for compensation is a tax return preparer.
questions.explanationJa:
申告書作成者（tax return preparer）とは、「報酬を得て」申告書や還付請求書を作成する（または作成させる）者をいう（IRC §7701(a)(36)）。Louis は無報酬のボランティアとして Form 990 を作成しているので、作成者には当たらない。
理事であることは判定に関係しない（報酬を受ければ理事でも作成者になる）。還付請求を含むかどうかも無関係で、定義は申告書と還付請求の両方を含む。非営利団体の申告書が作成者規制の対象外ということもなく、報酬を得て Form 990 を作れば作成者になる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.3 (AICPA No. 9843)

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer agreed to a finding of fraud on an income tax return filed two years ago. What is the maximum time limitation, if any, after which the IRS may not assess any additional taxes against the taxpayer for this tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Three years

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is no time limitation

questions.explanation:
The general assessment period is three years after the return is filed (IRC §6501(a)). However, under IRC §6501(c)(1), in the case of a false or fraudulent return with intent to evade tax, the tax may be assessed at any time. Because the taxpayer agreed to a finding of fraud, there is no time limitation on assessing additional tax for that return.

One year and two years are not assessment periods that apply to income tax deficiencies.
Three years is the general rule, which does not apply to a fraudulent return.
questions.explanationJa:
更正（追加税額の賦課）の期限は原則として申告から3年（IRC §6501(a)）だが、脱税目的の虚偽・不正な申告については期限が無く、いつでも賦課できる（§6501(c)(1)）。本問の納税者は不正（fraud）の認定に同意しているので、期限は無い。
1年・2年は所得税の賦課期限ではない。3年は原則の期限であり、不正申告には適用されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.7 (AICPA No. 9847)

questions.stem: Under the position taken by a majority of the courts, to which third parties will an accountant who negligently prepares a client's financial report be liable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only those third parties in privity of contract with the accountant

choices.label: B
choices.text: All third parties who relied on the report and sustained injury

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any foreseen or known third party who relied on the report

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any third party whose reliance on the report was reasonably foreseeable

questions.explanation:
Under the majority approach (Restatement (Second) of Torts §552), an accountant who negligently prepares a report is liable to the client and to third parties whose reliance was actually foreseen: persons, or a limited group of persons, whom the accountant knew would receive and rely on the report for the transaction involved. The same common law rules govern a tax return preparer's liability for negligence to third parties.

Limiting liability only to parties in privity of contract is the minority Ultramares approach.
Liability to all third parties who relied and were injured is broader than any recognized negligence standard; such broad liability applies only to fraud.
Liability to any third party whose reliance was reasonably foreseeable is the minority (Rosenblum) approach.
questions.explanationJa:
過失による報告書の作成について、多数派の立場（Restatement (Second) of Torts §552）では、会計士は依頼人のほか、その報告書を受け取り依拠することを会計士が知っていた、または予見していた（foreseen）第三者に対して責任を負う。申告書作成者の過失責任も同じコモンローの規律による。
契約関係（privity）のある者に限る立場は少数派の Ultramares 法理。依拠して損害を受けた全ての第三者への責任は詐欺の場合の範囲である。合理的に予見可能な（foreseeable）第三者全てに広げるのは少数派の Rosenblum 法理。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.21 (AICPA No. 9961)

questions.stem: Which of the following is not considered a primary authoritative source when conducting tax research?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Internal Revenue Code

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tax Court cases

choices.label: C
choices.text: IRS publications

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treasury regulations

questions.explanation:
Primary authority consists of the sources of tax law themselves: the Internal Revenue Code (statutory), Treasury Regulations and other official administrative pronouncements such as revenue rulings and revenue procedures, and judicial decisions such as Tax Court cases. IRS publications are informational guides written for taxpayers; they are not binding on the IRS or taxpayers and are not authoritative sources for tax research.

The Internal Revenue Code is the highest primary statutory authority.
Tax Court cases are primary judicial authority.
Treasury Regulations are primary administrative authority interpreting the Code.
questions.explanationJa:
一次的権威（primary authority）とは、内国歳入法典（IRC）、財務省規則・歳入規則などの公式な行政上の規定、租税裁判所などの判決といった、税法そのものの法源をいう。IRS の出版物（publications）は納税者向けの案内であり、IRS も納税者も拘束されず、権威ある法源ではない。
IRC は最上位の制定法、租税裁判所の判決は判例上の一次的権威、財務省規則は IRC を解釈する行政上の一次的権威である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.9 (AICPA No. 89809)

questions.stem: An IRS agent has just completed an examination of a corporation and issued a "no change" report. Which of the following statements about that situation is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The taxpayer may not amend the tax return for that taxable year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The IRS generally does not reopen the examination except in cases involving fraud or other similar misrepresentation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The IRS may not reopen the examination.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The IRS may not examine any other tax return of the corporation for a period of one year.

questions.explanation:
When an examination is closed with a "no change" report, IRS policy (Rev. Proc. 2005-32) is not to reopen the closed case to make an adjustment unfavorable to the taxpayer except where there is evidence of fraud, malfeasance, collusion, concealment or misrepresentation of a material fact, a clearly defined substantial error based on an established IRS position, or other circumstances indicating that failure to reopen would be a serious administrative omission.

A no change report does not prevent the taxpayer from filing an amended return for that year.
The IRS may reopen the examination in the limited circumstances described above, so it is not absolutely barred.
A no change report on one return does not bar the IRS from examining the corporation's other returns for any period.
questions.explanationJa:
調査が「是正事項なし（no change）」で終了した場合、IRS は原則として納税者に不利な方向で調査を再開しない。例外は、不正（fraud）、共謀、重要な事実の隠蔽・虚偽表示、IRS の確立した立場に基づく明白で重大な誤りなどがある場合に限られる（Rev. Proc. 2005-32）。
no change でも納税者は修正申告できる。上記の例外があるので IRS が絶対に再開できないわけではない。他の年度の申告書を1年間調査できないという制限も無い。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.17 (AICPA No. 89817)

questions.stem: Under Treasury Circular 230, which of the following actions of a CPA tax advisor is characteristic of a best practice in rendering tax advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Requesting written evidence from a client that the fee proposal for tax advice has been approved by the board of directors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recommending to the client that the advisor’s tax advice be made orally instead of in a written memorandum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Establishing relevant facts, evaluating the reasonableness of assumptions and representations, and arriving at a conclusion supported by the law and facts in a tax memorandum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Requiring the client to supply a written representation, signed under penalties of perjury, concerning the facts and statements provided to the CPA for preparing a tax memorandum

questions.explanation:
Circular 230 §10.33 describes best practices for tax advisors. In providing advice and preparing submissions, a practitioner should communicate clearly with the client about the terms of the engagement, establish the facts, determine which facts are relevant, evaluate the reasonableness of any assumptions or representations, relate the applicable law (including potentially applicable judicial doctrines) to the relevant facts, and arrive at a conclusion supported by the law and the facts.

Obtaining written evidence that the board approved the fee proposal is not one of the best practices listed in §10.33.
Recommending oral rather than written advice is not a best practice; Circular 230 does not favor oral advice.
Requiring a written representation signed under penalties of perjury is not a Circular 230 best practice; practitioners may generally rely in good faith on client information without such a statement.
questions.explanationJa:
Circular 230 §10.33 は税務助言のベストプラクティスとして、業務条件の明確な伝達、事実の確定と関連する事実の判断、前提・表明の合理性の評価、適用法令（判例法理を含む）と事実の関連付け、法令と事実に裏付けられた結論の導出を挙げている。
取締役会による報酬承認の書面の入手、書面ではなく口頭での助言の推奨、偽証罪の罰則付きの書面による表明の要求は、いずれも §10.33 のベストプラクティスに含まれない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.19 (AICPA No. 89819)

questions.stem: A CPA prepared a tax return for a client who will receive a refund check. The client is traveling abroad and asked the CPA to pick up the check at the client's home address. Under Treasury Circular 230, any of the following actions, if taken by the CPA relating to the refund check, would be a violation of the rules of practice before the Internal Revenue Service, except

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endorsing the check and depositing it into the client’s bank account

choices.label: B
choices.text: Holding the check for safe keeping and awaiting the client’s return

choices.label: C
choices.text: Holding the check until the client is billed, then endorsing and depositing the check into the CPA’s account as payment for the bill

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endorsing the check and depositing it into an escrow account for the client’s benefit

questions.explanation:
Circular 230 §10.31 provides that a practitioner who prepares tax returns may not endorse or otherwise negotiate any check (including directing or accepting payment by any means, electronic or otherwise, into an account owned or controlled by the practitioner) issued to a client by the government in respect of a federal tax liability. Merely holding the client's refund check for safekeeping until the client returns does not endorse or negotiate the check and is therefore not a violation.

Endorsing the check and depositing it into the client's bank account is negotiating the check, which §10.31 prohibits.
Endorsing the check and depositing it into the CPA's own account as payment of the bill is a prohibited negotiation of the client's refund.
Endorsing the check and depositing it into an escrow account is still an endorsement and negotiation of the client's refund check.
questions.explanationJa:
Circular 230 §10.31 は、申告書を作成する実務家が、連邦税に関して政府から依頼人に発行された小切手に裏書し、またはその他の方法で換金（自分が所有・管理する口座への入金を含む）することを禁じている。依頼人の帰国まで還付小切手を保管しておくだけなら裏書も換金もしていないので違反にならない。
裏書して依頼人の口座に入金すること、裏書して報酬の支払いとして CPA 自身の口座に入金すること、裏書してエスクロー口座に入金することは、いずれも小切手の裏書・換金に当たり違反となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.20 (AICPA No. 89820)

questions.stem: In which of the following circumstances does the three-year statute of limitations on additional tax assessments apply?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A taxpayer willfully attempts to evade tax in filing income tax returns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A taxpayer inadvertently omits from gross income an amount in excess of 25% of the gross income stated on the income tax return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A taxpayer inadvertently overstates deductions equal to 15% of gross income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The IRS files a substitute income tax return when it learns that a taxpayer failed to file a return.

questions.explanation:
The general three-year assessment period of IRC §6501(a) applies unless an exception applies. Overstating deductions, even significantly, does not extend the period, because the six-year rule of §6501(e) applies only to omissions of gross income exceeding 25% of the gross income stated on the return. An inadvertent overstatement of deductions equal to 15% of gross income is therefore subject to the three-year statute.

A willful attempt to evade tax (fraud) allows assessment at any time (§6501(c)(1)).
An omission of gross income exceeding 25% of the gross income stated on the return extends the period to six years (§6501(e)(1)).
A substitute return prepared by the IRS does not start the statute of limitations, so when the taxpayer fails to file, tax may be assessed at any time (§6501(c)(3), (b)(3)).
questions.explanationJa:
賦課期限は原則3年（IRC §6501(a)）。6年に延びるのは申告書記載の総所得の25%を超える所得の申告漏れの場合（§6501(e)）であり、控除の過大計上は対象外。したがって総所得の15%に当たる控除の過大計上には3年の期限が適用される。
故意の脱税（fraud）は期限なし（§6501(c)(1)）。25%超の所得の申告漏れは6年。無申告の場合は IRS が代替申告書を作成しても期限は進行せず、いつでも賦課できる（§6501(c)(3)、(b)(3)）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.33 (AICPA No. 89833)

questions.stem: Tax return preparers can be subject to penalties under the Internal Revenue Code for failure to do any of the following, except

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sign a tax return as a preparer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disclose a conflict of interest

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provide a client with a copy of the tax return

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep a record of returns prepared

questions.explanation:
IRC §6695 imposes penalties on tax return preparers who fail to furnish a copy of the return to the taxpayer (§6695(a)), fail to sign the return (§6695(b)), fail to furnish an identifying number (§6695(c)), fail to retain a copy or list of returns prepared (§6695(d)), or fail to meet due diligence requirements for certain credits and head of household status (§6695(g)). The Code contains no preparer penalty for failing to disclose a conflict of interest; conflicts of interest are addressed by Circular 230 §10.29, which is enforced through disciplinary sanctions rather than Code penalties.

Failing to sign a return as preparer is penalized under §6695(b).
Failing to provide the client with a copy of the return is penalized under §6695(a).
Failing to keep a record (copy or list) of returns prepared is penalized under §6695(d).
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §6695 は申告書作成者に対し、納税者への写しの交付漏れ（(a)）、署名漏れ（(b)）、識別番号の記載漏れ（(c)）、作成した申告書の写し・一覧の保存漏れ（(d)）、一定の税額控除や世帯主区分に関するデューデリジェンス違反（(g)）について罰則を課す。利益相反の開示漏れについての IRC 上の罰則は無く、利益相反は Circular 230 §10.29 の問題として懲戒処分の対象となる。
署名漏れ・写しの交付漏れ・記録の保存漏れは、いずれも §6695 の罰則の対象である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.36 (AICPA No. 89836)

questions.stem: A CPA assists a taxpayer in tax planning regarding a transaction that meets the definition of a tax shelter as defined in the Internal Revenue Code. Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, the CPA should inform the taxpayer of the penalty risks unless the transaction, at the minimum, meets which of the following standards for being sustained if challenged?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More likely than not

choices.label: B
choices.text: Not frivolous

choices.label: C
choices.text: Realistic possibility

choices.label: D
choices.text: Substantial authority

questions.explanation:
Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, a CPA should advise the taxpayer of the potential penalty consequences of a recommended tax position. For a tax shelter as defined in IRC §6662(d)(2), the substantial understatement penalty cannot be avoided by disclosure or by substantial authority alone. The taxpayer avoids the penalty only if the treatment is supported by substantial authority and the taxpayer reasonably believed the treatment was more likely than not proper (Treas. Reg. §1.6662-4(g)). The CPA should therefore inform the taxpayer of the penalty risk unless the transaction meets, at a minimum, the more likely than not standard.

Not frivolous is a much lower standard and does not protect a tax shelter item from the penalty.
Realistic possibility is lower than more likely than not and does not protect a tax shelter item from the penalty.
Substantial authority alone is not sufficient for a tax shelter item, because the taxpayer must also reasonably believe that the position is more likely than not proper.
questions.explanationJa:
SSTS では、CPA は推奨する税務ポジションについて生じうるペナルティを納税者に知らせる。IRC §6662(d)(2) のタックスシェルターに当たる取引では、開示や substantial authority だけでは過少申告ペナルティを避けられず、substantial authority に加えて「more likely than not（50%超の可能性で認められる）」と合理的に信じていることが必要（Treas. Reg. §1.6662-4(g)）。したがって、少なくとも more likely than not を満たさない限り、ペナルティのリスクを知らせるべきである。
not frivolous や realistic possibility は more likely than not より低い基準で、タックスシェルターのペナルティを防げない。substantial authority だけでも足りず、more likely than not と信じていることが必要。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.37 (AICPA No. 89837)

questions.stem: Which Senate committee considers new tax legislation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budget

choices.label: B
choices.text: Finance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Appropriations

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rules and Administration

questions.explanation:
Revenue bills must originate in the House of Representatives (U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 7), where tax legislation is considered by the House Ways and Means Committee. The bill then goes to the Senate, where the Senate Finance Committee considers it. Differences between the House and Senate versions are resolved by a conference committee. The reports of the Ways and Means Committee, the Senate Finance Committee and the conference committee form the legislative history used in interpreting the Internal Revenue Code.

The Senate Budget Committee develops the congressional budget resolution; it does not consider the substance of tax bills.
The Senate Appropriations Committee handles spending (appropriations) bills, not revenue legislation.
The Senate Rules and Administration Committee handles Senate rules, administration and federal elections, not tax legislation.
questions.explanationJa:
歳入法案は下院から提出しなければならず（合衆国憲法第1条第7節）、下院では歳入委員会（Ways and Means Committee）が審議する。その後、上院では財政委員会（Finance Committee）が審議し、上下両院の違いは両院協議会で調整する。これらの委員会報告は、IRC を解釈する際の立法経緯として使われる。
予算委員会は予算決議を作成する委員会、歳出委員会は歳出法案を扱う委員会、議事運営委員会は上院の規則・運営・選挙を扱う委員会で、いずれも税法案を審議しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.39 (AICPA No. 89839)

questions.stem: A CPA prepares a client's tax return containing business travel expenses without inquiring about the existence of documentation for the expenses. Which statement best describes the consequence of the CPA's lack of inquiry?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The CPA may be assessed a tax return preparer penalty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA may be charged with preparing a fraudulent return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The client will not owe an understatement penalty if the return is audited and the expenses disallowed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The client will not be subject to a fraud penalty.

questions.explanation:
A tax return preparer may generally rely in good faith on information furnished by the client, but under Treas. Reg. §1.6694-1(e)(1) the preparer must make appropriate inquiries if the Code or regulations require specific facts or substantiation as a condition of a deduction. Travel expenses are subject to the strict substantiation rules of IRC §274(d), so a preparer who claims them without asking whether the required documentation exists has not acted reasonably and may be assessed a preparer penalty under IRC §6694(a) if the resulting position leads to an understatement. Circular 230 §10.34(d) similarly requires reasonable inquiries.

Preparing a fraudulent return requires willful or intentional conduct; a mere failure to inquire is negligence, not fraud. The client is not protected from an accuracy-related understatement penalty simply because the preparer failed to inquire; the client remains responsible for substantiating the deductions. Likewise, the preparer's lack of inquiry does not shield the client from a fraud penalty if the client acted fraudulently.
questions.explanationJa:
申告書作成者は原則として顧客の情報を善意で信頼してよいが、Treas. Reg. §1.6694-1(e)(1)により、法令が控除の要件として特定の事実や立証書類を求める場合には適切な質問をしなければならない。旅費は§274(d)の厳格な立証要件の対象であり、書類の有無を確認せずに計上した作成者は合理的に行動したとはいえず、過少申告につながれば§6694(a)の作成者罰則を課されうる。Circular 230 §10.34(d)も合理的な質問を求めている。

不正申告書の作成には故意が必要で、確認を怠っただけでは過失にとどまる。作成者が確認しなかったからといって顧客が過少申告ペナルティを免れることはなく、立証責任は顧客にある。同様に、顧客自身に詐欺があれば詐欺ペナルティも免れない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. 90212)

questions.stem: Under Treasury Circular 230, in which of the following situations is a CPA prohibited from giving written advice concerning one or more federal tax issues?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The CPA takes into account the possibility that a tax return will not be audited.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA reasonably relies upon representations of the client.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The CPA considers all relevant facts that are known.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The CPA takes into consideration assumptions about future events related to the relevant facts.

questions.explanation:
Circular 230 §10.37(a)(2) sets the standards for written advice concerning federal tax matters. The practitioner must base the advice on reasonable factual and legal assumptions (including assumptions about future events), reasonably consider all relevant facts the practitioner knows or reasonably should know, may rely on representations of the client unless reliance is unreasonable, and must not, in evaluating a federal tax matter, take into account the possibility that a tax return will not be audited or that a matter will not be raised on audit. Taking audit risk into account is therefore prohibited.

Reasonably relying on the client's representations is permitted. Considering all relevant known facts is required. Making reasonable assumptions about future events is permitted.
questions.explanationJa:
Circular 230 §10.37(a)(2)は書面による税務助言の基準を定める。実務家は、合理的な事実上・法律上の前提（将来事象に関する前提を含む）に基づき、知っている又は知るべき関連事実をすべて考慮し、不合理でない限り顧客の表明に依拠できる。一方、申告書が調査されない可能性や調査で問題にされない可能性を考慮してはならない。したがって調査されない可能性を考慮することが禁止される。

顧客の表明に合理的に依拠することは認められる。既知の関連事実をすべて考慮することは求められる。将来事象に関する前提を置くことも認められる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.14 (AICPA No. 90214)

questions.stem: In year 6, an IRS agent completed an examination of a corporation's year 5 tax return and proposed an adjustment that will result in an increase in taxable income for each of years 1 through year 5. All returns were filed on the original due date. The proposed adjustment relates to the disallowance of corporate jet usage for personal reasons. The agent does not find the error to be fraudulent or substantial in nature. Which of the following statements regarding this adjustment is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The adjustment is improper because an agent may only propose adjustments to the year under examination.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The adjustment is proper because there is no statute of limitations for improperly claiming personal expenses as business expenses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The adjustment is proper because it relates to a change in accounting method, which can be made retroactively irrespective of the statute of limitations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The adjustment is improper because the statute of limitations has expired for several years of the adjustment.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6501(a), the IRS generally must assess additional tax within 3 years after the return was filed (a return filed early is treated as filed on the due date). The 6-year period under §6501(e) applies only to a substantial omission of income (more than 25% of gross income reported), and there is no limitation period for fraudulent returns under §6501(c). The agent found the error to be neither fraudulent nor substantial, so the 3-year period applies. Because the examination was completed in year 6 and all returns were filed on their original due dates, the limitation periods for the earlier years covered by the adjustment have already expired, and those years cannot be assessed.

An agent is not limited to the year under examination; adjustments may be proposed for other open years. There is no unlimited period for claiming personal expenses as business expenses absent fraud. Disallowing personal use of a corporate jet is a correction of an improper deduction, not a change in accounting method.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §6501(a)により、IRSは原則として申告書提出後3年以内に追加税額を賦課しなければならない（期限前提出は期限日に提出したものとみなす）。§6501(e)の6年は総所得の25%超の申告漏れがある場合に限られ、§6501(c)により不正申告には時効がない。本問では不正でも多額でもないので3年が適用される。year 6年に調査が終わり、すべて期限どおりに提出されているので、調整対象のうち古い年度は3年の時効が完成しており賦課できない。

調査官は調査対象年度以外の未時効年度についても調整を提案できる。不正がない限り、私的費用の事業費計上に時効がないということはない。社用ジェットの私的使用の否認は不適切な控除の是正であり、会計方法の変更ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.26 (AICPA No. 90226)

questions.stem: Joe is the trustee of a trust set up for his father. Under the Internal Revenue Code, when Joe prepares the annual trust tax return, Form 1041, he

choices.label: A
choices.text: Must obtain the written permission of the beneficiary prior to signing as a tax return preparer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Is not considered a tax return preparer

choices.label: C
choices.text: May not sign the return unless he receives additional compensation for the tax return

choices.label: D
choices.text: Is considered a tax return preparer because his father is the grantor of the trust

questions.explanation:
IRC §7701(a)(36) defines a tax return preparer as a person who prepares for compensation all or a substantial portion of a return or refund claim, but it expressly excludes a person who prepares a return or claim for refund as a fiduciary for another person (see also Treas. Reg. §301.7701-15(f)). Because Joe prepares the trust's Form 1041 in his capacity as trustee, he is acting as a fiduciary and is not a tax return preparer.

No written permission from the beneficiary is required for a trustee to sign the trust's return. Additional compensation is not a condition of signing; the trustee signs the return as fiduciary. The fact that Joe's father is the grantor does not make Joe a tax return preparer; the fiduciary exclusion applies regardless of the family relationship.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §7701(a)(36)は、報酬を得て申告書の全部又は相当部分を作成する者を申告書作成者と定義するが、受託者（fiduciary）として他者の申告書・還付請求を作成する者を明示的に除外している（Treas. Reg. §301.7701-15(f)も参照）。Joeは受託者としてForm 1041を作成するので、申告書作成者に当たらない。

受託者が信託の申告書に署名するのに受益者の書面による許可は不要。追加報酬の受領も署名の条件ではなく、受託者として署名する。父親が設定者であることは申告書作成者に該当する理由にならず、親族関係に関係なく受託者除外が適用される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.35 (AICPA No. 90235)

questions.stem: An individual paid taxes 27 months ago, but did not file a tax return for that year. Now the individual wants to file a claim for refund of federal income taxes that were paid at that time. The individual must file the claim for refund within which of the following time periods after those taxes were paid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Three years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Four years

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6511(a), a claim for refund must be filed within 3 years from the time the return was filed or 2 years from the time the tax was paid, whichever period expires later; if no return was filed by the taxpayer, the claim must be filed within 2 years from the time the tax was paid. Because the individual did not file a return for that year, the 2-year-from-payment period applies.

One year is not a refund limitation period under §6511(a). Three years is measured from the filing of a return, which requires that a return was filed. Four years is not the refund claim period.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §6511(a)により、還付請求は申告書の提出から3年又は納付から2年のいずれか遅い方までに行わなければならず、納税者が申告書を提出していない場合は納付から2年以内に行わなければならない。本問では当該年度の申告書を提出していないので、納付から2年が適用される。

1年は§6511(a)の還付請求期間ではない。3年は申告書提出時から起算するもので、申告書の提出が前提となる。4年も還付請求期間ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.40 (AICPA No. 90240)

questions.stem: Shore, a paid tax return preparer, was given three partnership Schedule K-1 forms by client Fuller. Fuller is a limited partner in each of the partnerships. The K-1s disclosed small pass-through losses allocated to Fuller. Fuller had passive income in excess of these losses from other partnerships. According to the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, assuming that no at-risk limitations apply, what is Shore's professional responsibility regarding the reporting of these partnership losses on Fuller's federal income tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To verify the client’s basis by examining client’s records from the initial investment to the present

choices.label: B
choices.text: To accept the information without further inquiry unless Shore has reason to believe that the information is incorrect

choices.label: C
choices.text: To verify the initial investment in each partnership entity unless Shore has reason to believe that the information is incorrect

choices.label: D
choices.text: To request the complete partnership returns of the partnership entities unless Shore has reason to believe that the information is incorrect

questions.explanation:
Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services on the procedural aspects of preparing returns, a member may in good faith rely, without verification, on information furnished by the taxpayer or by third parties. The member should not ignore the implications of information furnished and should make reasonable inquiries if the information appears to be incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent. Information on Schedules K-1 received from the partnerships may therefore be used without further inquiry unless Shore has reason to believe it is incorrect. Circular 230 §10.34(d) contains a similar reliance rule.

Examining the client's records from the initial investment to the present to verify basis, verifying the initial investment in each partnership, and requesting the complete partnership returns all describe verification procedures that the standards do not require in the absence of a reason to doubt the information.
questions.explanationJa:
AICPAの税務業務基準書（SSTS）の申告書作成手続に関する基準では、会員は納税者や第三者から提供された情報を検証せずに善意で信頼してよい。ただし提供情報の意味を無視してはならず、情報が誤り・不完全・矛盾していると思われる場合には合理的な質問をすべきである。したがって、パートナーシップから受け取ったK-1の情報は、誤りと信じる理由がない限りそのまま使用できる。Circular 230 §10.34(d)にも同様の規定がある。

当初投資から現在までの記録を調べてベーシスを検証すること、各パートナーシップへの当初投資額を検証すること、パートナーシップの申告書一式を取り寄せることは、いずれも情報を疑う理由がない限り基準上求められない検証手続である。
references: AICPA SSTS (Certain Procedural Aspects of Preparing Returns)
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.1 (AICPA No. 90551)

questions.stem: Which of the following bodies has the authority to suspend or revoke a CPA's license for acts discreditable to the profession?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The state society of certified public accountants

choices.label: B
choices.text: The state board of accountancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Public Company Accountancy Oversight Board

choices.label: D
choices.text: The American Institute of Certified Public Accountants

questions.explanation:
The CPA license is issued by the state board of accountancy, a governmental agency created by state law. Only the state board has the legal authority to suspend or revoke a license, including for acts discreditable to the profession (see the Uniform Accountancy Act provisions on board discipline).

A state society of CPAs is a voluntary professional association; it can expel or discipline its members but cannot revoke a license. The PCAOB regulates auditors of public companies and can bar a person from auditing public companies, but it does not issue or revoke state CPA licenses. The AICPA is a voluntary membership organization that can suspend or terminate membership but has no power over a license.
questions.explanationJa:
CPAの免許は州法に基づく行政機関である州会計士委員会（state board of accountancy）が付与する。職業の信用を損なう行為を理由とするものも含め、免許の停止・取消しの法的権限を持つのは州会計士委員会だけである（統一会計士法の懲戒規定参照）。

州CPA協会は任意の職業団体で、会員の除名等はできても免許は取り消せない。PCAOBは上場会社の監査人を監督し上場会社監査から排除できるが、州の免許を付与・取消しする権限はない。AICPAも任意加入団体で、会員資格の停止等はできても免許には権限がない。
references: Uniform Accountancy Act (state board of accountancy disciplinary authority)
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.2 (AICPA No. 90552)

questions.stem: Under the common law, which of the following defenses, if used by a CPA, would best avoid liability in an action for negligence brought by a client?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The client was contributory negligent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The client was comparatively negligent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The accuracy of the CPA’s report was not guaranteed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The CPA's negligence was not the proximate cause of the client’s losses.

questions.explanation:
To recover for common law negligence, the client must prove a duty of care, breach of that duty, actual loss, and that the CPA's breach was the proximate cause of the loss. Showing that the CPA's negligence was not the proximate cause of the client's losses defeats an essential element of the claim and therefore avoids liability entirely.

Contributory negligence by the client is a complete defense only in the few jurisdictions that retain it, and it applies only when the client's negligence contributed to the CPA's failure. Comparative negligence usually only reduces the damages in proportion to the client's fault rather than eliminating liability. Stating that the accuracy of the report was not guaranteed is not a defense; a CPA is held to the standard of reasonable care regardless of whether accuracy was guaranteed.
questions.explanationJa:
コモンロー上の過失責任を問うには、顧客は注意義務、その違反、現実の損害、そしてCPAの違反が損害の近因（proximate cause）であることを立証しなければならない。CPAの過失が損害の近因でないことを示せば、請求の必須要件が欠けるので責任を完全に免れる。

顧客の寄与過失が完全な抗弁となるのはそれを維持する少数の法域に限られ、顧客の過失がCPAの失敗に寄与した場合にしか使えない。比較過失は通常、顧客の過失割合に応じて損害額を減らすにとどまる。報告書の正確性を保証していないことは抗弁にならず、保証の有無にかかわらずCPAには合理的注意の基準が課される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.3 (AICPA No. 90553)

questions.stem: A taxpayer has had one issue under audit by the Internal Revenue Service for several years. Unless the taxpayer agrees otherwise, the IRS has at most how many years to assess taxes after the taxpayer's return was filed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Three

choices.label: B
choices.text: Four

choices.label: C
choices.text: Five

choices.label: D
choices.text: Seven

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6501(a), the IRS generally must assess tax within 3 years after the return was filed. The length of time an issue has been under audit does not extend this period. The period can be extended only by agreement of the taxpayer (a consent under IRC §6501(c)(4), such as Form 872), or by special rules that the facts do not indicate, such as a substantial omission of income or fraud.

Four years is not the general assessment period. Five years is not an assessment period under §6501. Seven years is not the assessment period either; six years applies only to a substantial omission of gross income.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §6501(a)により、IRSは原則として申告書提出後3年以内に賦課しなければならない。調査期間が長引いても期間は延びない。延長されるのは納税者の同意（§6501(c)(4)の合意、Form 872等）がある場合か、問題文にない総所得の多額な申告漏れや不正といった特則に該当する場合のみである。

4年・5年は§6501の賦課期間ではない。7年も賦課期間ではなく、総所得の多額な申告漏れの場合でも6年である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.8 (AICPA No. 90558)

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of elements must a client prove to hold an accountant liable for common law negligence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Freedom from contributory negligence and privity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breach of the accountant’s duty of care and loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: Willful misrepresentation and breach of the accountant's duty of care

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scienter and a violation of GMP

questions.explanation:
To hold an accountant liable for common law negligence, the client must prove (1) the accountant owed a duty of care, (2) the accountant breached that duty by failing to exercise the care of a reasonably prudent accountant, (3) the client suffered an actual loss, and (4) the breach proximately caused the loss. Breach of the duty of care and loss are therefore elements the client must prove.

Freedom from contributory negligence is not an element of the plaintiff's case; contributory negligence is a defense raised by the accountant, and a client is in privity with its accountant without needing to prove it separately. Willful misrepresentation is an element of fraud, not negligence. Scienter is likewise an element of fraud, not negligence.
questions.explanationJa:
会計士にコモンロー上の過失責任を問うには、顧客は①注意義務の存在、②合理的に慎重な会計士の注意を怠った義務違反、③現実の損害、④違反と損害の近因関係を立証しなければならない。したがって注意義務違反と損害は顧客が立証すべき要素である。

寄与過失がないことは原告の立証要素ではなく、会計士側の抗弁である。また顧客と会計士の間には当然に契約関係（privity）がある。故意の不実表示や悪意（scienter）は詐欺の要件であり、過失の要件ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.21 (AICPA No. 90571)

questions.stem: American Corp. retained Baker, CPA, to conduct an audit of its financial statements to obtain a bank line of credit. American signed an engagement letter drafted by Baker that included a disclaimer provision. As a result of Baker's failure to detect a material misstatement in American's financial statements, the audit report contained an unqualified opinion. Based on American's audited financial statements, National extended credit to American. American filed a petition in bankruptcy shortly thereafter. National sued Baker for damages based on common law fraud. What would be Baker's best defense?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Baker acted with due diligence in conducting the audit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Baker included a disclaimer provision in the engagement letter with American.

choices.label: C
choices.text: National was not in privity with Baker.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Baker lacked the intent to deceive.

questions.explanation:
Common law fraud requires a false representation of a material fact, scienter (knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard for the truth, i.e., intent to deceive), intent that the plaintiff rely, justifiable reliance, and resulting damages. Because scienter is an essential element, Baker's best defense to a fraud claim is that Baker lacked the intent to deceive; a failure to detect a misstatement through negligence alone is not fraud. Because fraud is an intentional tort, the accountant is liable to any person who justifiably relies, regardless of privity.

Acting with due diligence is a defense to negligence and to statutory claims, but the stronger and more direct defense to fraud is the absence of scienter. A disclaimer in the engagement letter with American does not bind National, a third party, and cannot shield an accountant from liability for fraud. Lack of privity is not a defense to fraud.
questions.explanationJa:
コモンロー上の詐欺の成立には、重要な事実の虚偽表示、悪意（scienter: 虚偽と知っている又は真実を無謀に無視した、すなわち欺く意図）、原告に依拠させる意図、正当な依拠、損害が必要である。悪意は必須要件なので、詐欺の請求に対するBakerの最善の抗弁は欺く意図がなかったことである。過失により虚偽表示を発見できなかっただけでは詐欺にならない。詐欺は故意の不法行為なので、契約関係の有無に関係なく正当に依拠した者に責任を負う。

相当の注意を尽くしたことは過失への抗弁だが、詐欺に対してはscienterの欠如がより直接的な抗弁となる。Americanとの契約書の免責条項は第三者Nationalを拘束せず、詐欺の責任を免れさせない。契約関係（privity）がないことは詐欺に対する抗弁にならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.22 (AICPA No. 90572)

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists the order, from earliest to latest, that U.S. legislative bodies consider new tax legislation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: House of Representatives, U.S. Senate, Joint Conference Committee

choices.label: B
choices.text: Joint Conference Committee, House of Representatives, Senate Finance Committee

choices.label: C
choices.text: U.S. Senate, Joint Conference Committee, House of Representatives

choices.label: D
choices.text: House of Representatives, Joint Conference Committee, U.S. Senate

questions.explanation:
Under Article I, Section 7 of the U.S. Constitution, all bills for raising revenue must originate in the House of Representatives. Tax legislation is first considered by the House Ways and Means Committee and passed by the full House, then considered by the Senate Finance Committee and passed by the full Senate. If the House and Senate versions differ, a Joint Conference Committee reconciles them, after which both chambers vote on the conference version before it goes to the President. The committee reports produced along the way are part of a statute's legislative history used in tax research.

The sequences that begin with the Joint Conference Committee or with the Senate are incorrect because revenue bills originate in the House and the conference committee acts only after both chambers have passed their versions. The sequence placing the Joint Conference Committee before the Senate is incorrect because the conference committee reconciles bills already passed by both chambers.
questions.explanationJa:
合衆国憲法第1条第7節により、歳入に関する法案は下院から発議しなければならない。税法案はまず下院歳入委員会で審議され下院本会議で可決された後、上院財政委員会で審議され上院本会議で可決される。両院の案が異なれば両院協議会が調整し、両院が協議会案を可決して大統領に送られる。この過程の委員会報告書は、税務調査で用いる立法経緯の資料となる。

両院協議会や上院から始まる順序は、歳入法案は下院から発議され、協議会は両院が可決した後に開かれるので誤り。両院協議会を上院より前に置く順序も、協議会は両院を通過した法案を調整するものなので誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.26 (AICPA No. 90576)

questions.stem: In which of the following circumstances would a tax return preparer be prohibited from disclosing a client's tax return information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The information will be needed for a peer review.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The information will be provided in response to a court order.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The information will be provided to a section 501(c)(3) charity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The information will be used to prepare state or local tax returns.

questions.explanation:
IRC §7216 makes it a crime for a tax return preparer to knowingly or recklessly disclose or use tax return information without the taxpayer's consent, except as permitted by the regulations. Providing a client's tax return information to a §501(c)(3) charity is not an exception, so it requires the taxpayer's written consent and is otherwise prohibited.

Treas. Reg. §301.7216-2 permits disclosure without consent in several situations, including disclosure for a quality or peer review, disclosure pursuant to a court order (or other provision of law), and use of the information to prepare the taxpayer's state or local tax returns.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §7216は、申告書作成者が納税者の同意なしに申告情報を故意または無謀に開示・使用することを、規則で認められた場合を除き刑事罰の対象とする。§501(c)(3)の慈善団体への提供は例外に当たらないため、納税者の書面同意が無ければ禁止される。

一方、Treas. Reg. §301.7216-2は、品質管理・ピアレビューのための開示、裁判所命令（その他法令）に基づく開示、同じ納税者の州・地方税申告書の作成のための使用を、同意なしで認めている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.2 (AICPA No. 90802)

questions.stem: Under the Statements on Standards for Tax Services, what is a CPA's responsibility for verifying information furnished by the taxpayer or third parties?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A CPA need not make additional inquiries if the information furnished appears to be incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent with other facts known to the CPA.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A CPA need not consider implications of information furnished if the information comes directly from a third party.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A CPA may, in good faith, rely on information furnished by the taxpayer or by third parties without verification.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A CPA should not refer to the taxpayer’s previous tax returns unless the returns report transactions that affect the current tax period.

questions.explanation:
Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services (procedural aspects of preparing returns), a member may in good faith rely, without verification, on information furnished by the taxpayer or by third parties. Circular 230 §10.34(d) contains a similar rule for practitioners.

This reliance has limits. A CPA should not ignore the implications of information furnished and should make reasonable inquiries if the information appears to be incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent, either on its face or with other facts known to the CPA. That applies whether the information comes from the taxpayer or directly from a third party. The CPA should also refer to the taxpayer's prior-year returns whenever feasible, not only when they report transactions affecting the current period.
questions.explanationJa:
AICPAの税務業務基準（SSTS：申告書作成の手続的側面）では、CPAは納税者や第三者から提供された情報を、善意であれば検証せずに信頼してよい。Circular 230 §10.34(d)にも同様の規定がある。

ただし限界がある。提供情報が誤り・不完全・他の事実と矛盾しているように見える場合は、その意味を無視せず合理的な質問を行う必要があり、情報が第三者から直接来た場合でも同じである。また、前年度の申告書は可能な限り参照すべきであり、当期に影響する取引がある場合に限られるわけではない。
references: AICPA SSTS — Certain Procedural Aspects of Preparing Returns (former SSTS No. 3)
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.3 (AICPA No. 90803)

questions.stem: The IRS requested client records from a CPA who does not have possession or control of the records. According to Treasury Circular 230, the CPA must

choices.label: A
choices.text: Notify the IRS of the identity of any person who, according to the CPA’s belief, could have the records

choices.label: B
choices.text: Require the client to submit the records to the IRS or withdraw from the engagement

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain the records from the client and submit them to the IRS

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contact all third parties associated with the records, such as banks and employers, to obtain the requested records for submission to the IRS

questions.explanation:
Under Circular 230 §10.20(a), a practitioner must promptly submit records or information in any matter before the IRS upon a proper and lawful request by an IRS officer or employee. If the requested records are not in the practitioner's possession or control, the practitioner must promptly notify the requesting IRS officer or employee and provide any information the practitioner has regarding the identity of any person who the practitioner reasonably believes may have possession or control of the records.

Circular 230 does not require the practitioner to obtain the records from the client and submit them, to force the client to submit them or withdraw, or to contact banks, employers, and other third parties to collect the records.
questions.explanationJa:
Circular 230 §10.20(a)により、実務家はIRS職員から適法な請求があれば記録・情報を速やかに提出しなければならない。請求された記録を保有・支配していない場合は、速やかにIRS職員にその旨を通知し、記録を保有・支配していると合理的に考える者の身元について知っている情報を提供しなければならない。

Circular 230は、顧客から記録を取り寄せて提出すること、顧客に提出させるか辞任すること、銀行や雇用主など第三者に連絡して記録を集めることまでは求めていない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.21 (AICPA No. 90821)

questions.stem: Under Treasury Circular 230, which of the following correctly represents the requirements related to the communication of fee information from a tax practitioner to a taxpayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It may be communicated only through the confidential engagement letter between the tax practitioner and the taxpayer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It may be communicated in a number of ways, including in professional lists, telephone directories, mailings, and electronic mail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It must be communicated as an estimate before the engagement begins, with the understanding that the actual amount of the fee will not be determined until the engagement ends.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It may not be communicated by television, radio, or hand-delivered flyers.

questions.explanation:
Circular 230 §10.30 permits a practitioner to publish and communicate fee information (fixed fees, hourly rates, ranges of fees, and the availability of a written fee schedule). Under §10.30(b), fee information may be communicated in professional lists, telephone directories, print media, mailings, electronic mail, facsimile, hand-delivered flyers, radio, television, and any other method, provided the communication is not false, fraudulent, or coercive.

Fee information is therefore not limited to a confidential engagement letter, is not required to be given as a pre-engagement estimate, and may be communicated by television, radio, and hand-delivered flyers.
questions.explanationJa:
Circular 230 §10.30は、実務家が報酬情報（固定報酬、時間単価、報酬の幅、書面の報酬表の有無）を公表・伝達することを認めている。§10.30(b)により、虚偽・詐欺的・強要的でなければ、専門家名簿、電話帳、印刷媒体、郵送、電子メール、ファックス、手渡しのチラシ、ラジオ、テレビその他あらゆる方法で伝達できる。

したがって、守秘の契約書だけに限られることはなく、契約前に見積りとして示す義務も無く、テレビ・ラジオ・手渡しのチラシでも伝達できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.22 (AICPA No. 90822)

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to take a position on a tax return that the CPA determines is frivolous. However, the CPA and the taxpayer determine that the possibility of the return being selected for audit is remote and that even if the return is selected for audit the issue most likely will not be raised. According to the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, under these circumstances the CPA

choices.label: A
choices.text: Can sign or prepare the return with this position as long as the CPA advises the taxpayer that the position is frivolous

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cannot sign or prepare the return with this position

choices.label: C
choices.text: Can sign or prepare the return with this position because there is a realistic possibility that the position will not be challenged

choices.label: D
choices.text: Can sign or prepare the return with this position if the taxpayer signs a tax preparer waiver of liability

questions.explanation:
Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services on tax return positions, a member should not recommend a position or prepare or sign a return taking a position unless the member has a good-faith belief that the position meets the applicable standard (at a minimum a reasonable basis, with disclosure where the federal penalty rules require it). A frivolous position never meets these standards. The standards also state that the likelihood of audit or detection (the "audit lottery") may not be taken into account in deciding whether a position is supportable. The CPA therefore cannot sign or prepare the return with this position.

Advising the taxpayer that the position is frivolous does not cure the problem. The remote chance of audit is irrelevant, so it does not make the position supportable. A waiver of liability signed by the taxpayer does not permit the CPA to violate the professional standards (and frivolous positions also expose the preparer to penalties under IRC §6694 and Circular 230).
questions.explanationJa:
AICPAの税務業務基準（SSTS：申告ポジション）では、そのポジションが適用される基準（最低限、合理的根拠があること。連邦の罰則規定が開示を求める場合は開示も必要）を満たすと善意で信じられない限り、CPAはそのポジションを推奨したり、それを含む申告書を作成・署名したりしてはならない。根拠の無い（frivolous）ポジションはこの基準を満たさない。また、調査に選ばれる可能性・発見される可能性（いわゆる audit lottery）を判断に入れてはならない。したがってCPAはこの申告書を作成・署名できない。

ポジションが根拠の無いものであると納税者に伝えても問題は解消しない。調査の可能性が低いことは判断材料にできないので、それによってポジションが支持可能になるわけでもない。納税者が責任免除書に署名しても基準違反は許されず、IRC §6694やCircular 230上の罰則の対象にもなる。
references: AICPA SSTS — Tax Return Positions (former SSTS No. 1)
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.23 (AICPA No. 90823)

questions.stem: A CPA is researching a tax issue and is attempting to understand the intent of Congress. Which of the following would generally be least useful for that purpose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A Committee Report of the House Ways and Means Committee.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A Notice of Proposed Rulemaking.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A Senate Finance Committee Report

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Congressional Record.

questions.explanation:
Legislative history, which explains Congress's intent in enacting a provision, includes the House Ways and Means Committee reports, the Senate Finance Committee reports, conference committee reports, and floor debates published in the Congressional Record. A Notice of Proposed Rulemaking is issued by the Treasury Department (under its authority in IRC §7805) to propose regulations. It reflects the Treasury's interpretation of the law, not the intent of Congress, so it is the least useful of these sources for that purpose.

The House Ways and Means Committee report, the Senate Finance Committee report, and the Congressional Record are all part of the legislative history and are used to understand Congressional intent.
questions.explanationJa:
立法時の議会の意図を示す立法史には、下院歳入委員会報告書、上院財政委員会報告書、両院協議会報告書、議会議事録（Congressional Record）に載る本会議の討論が含まれる。規則制定案の告示（Notice of Proposed Rulemaking）は財務省がIRC §7805の権限に基づき規則案を示すもので、財務省の法解釈を表すにすぎず議会の意図を示すものではないため、この目的には最も役に立たない。

下院歳入委員会報告書、上院財政委員会報告書、議会議事録はいずれも立法史の一部で、議会の意図を理解するために使われる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2016 Recently Released Q.6 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A single-member LLC engages a CPA to prepare the year 2 income tax return. In the course of preparing the tax return, the CPA discovers that a partnership return was filed for year 1. Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, which of the following statements is not true regarding the CPA's duties upon discovering an error in filing the year 1 partnership return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The CPA must inform the client that an incorrect return was filed; under the AICPA standard, the CPA has the duty to report the error to the taxpayer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA should make sure the LLC files the correct return for year 2; under the AICPA standard, the CPA has the duty to take reasonable steps not to repeat the error.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The CPA must inform the IRS that the LLC filed an incorrect tax return for year 1; under the AICPA standard, the CPA has the duty to report the error to all relevant taxing agencies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The CPA should let the LLC decide whether it wants to correct the error; under the AICPA standard, the CPA has the duty to let the LLC make the decision to correct the error.

questions.explanation:
Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services on knowledge of error, a member who becomes aware of an error in a previously filed return should inform the taxpayer promptly of the error and recommend corrective measures. The member is not obligated to inform the taxing authority and may not do so without the taxpayer's permission, except where required by law. Circular 230 §10.21 likewise requires the practitioner to advise the client of the noncompliance and its consequences, not to notify the IRS. The statement that the CPA must inform the IRS of the year 1 error is therefore not true.

The other statements are true. The CPA must inform the client of the error. When continuing the engagement, the CPA should take reasonable steps to ensure the error is not repeated, so the correct return should be filed for year 2. Whether to correct the year 1 return is the taxpayer's decision.
questions.explanationJa:
AICPAの税務業務基準（SSTS：誤りの認識）では、CPAは過去に提出された申告書の誤りを知った場合、速やかに納税者に知らせ、是正措置を勧めるべきである。税務当局へ知らせる義務は無く、法律で求められる場合を除き納税者の許可なく知らせてはならない。Circular 230 §10.21も、顧客に不遵守とその結果を助言することを求めるだけで、IRSへの通知は求めていない。したがって「CPAはIRSに1年目の誤りを知らせなければならない」という記述が誤りである。

その他の記述は正しい。CPAは、誤りを顧客に知らせなければならない。業務を続ける場合は誤りを繰り返さないよう合理的な措置をとるべきで、2年目は正しい申告書を提出させる。1年目の申告を訂正するかどうかは納税者が決める。
references: AICPA SSTS — Knowledge of Error (former SSTS No. 6)
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2016 Recently Released Q.7 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a list of courts that are referred to as courts of original jurisdiction, or trial courts, for tax matters?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Tax Court, The U.S. District Court, and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Tax Court, the U.S. District Court, and the U.S. Bankruptcy Court.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Tax Court, the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, and the U.S. Court of Appeals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The U.S. District Court, the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, and the U.S. Court of Appeals.

questions.explanation:
A taxpayer may litigate a federal tax dispute in one of three trial-level courts (courts of original jurisdiction): the U.S. Tax Court (without first paying the deficiency), the U.S. District Court, or the U.S. Court of Federal Claims (both of which require paying the tax and suing for a refund).

The U.S. Courts of Appeals hear appeals from the trial courts and are not courts of original jurisdiction. Although a bankruptcy court can decide tax issues that arise in a bankruptcy case, it is not one of the three trial courts in which a taxpayer chooses to bring a tax dispute.
questions.explanationJa:
連邦税の争いを提起する第一審裁判所（original jurisdiction）は、租税裁判所（Tax Court、不足税額を納付せずに提訴可能）、連邦地方裁判所、連邦請求裁判所（後2者は納税後に還付訴訟を提起）の3つである。

連邦控訴裁判所は第一審裁判所からの上訴を扱う裁判所で、第一審裁判所ではない。破産裁判所は破産事件の中で税の問題を判断することがあるが、納税者が税務紛争を提起する3つの第一審裁判所には含まれない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2016 Recently Released Q.14 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: According to the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services, which of the following identifies the requirements for a tax advisor who believes that a taxpayer penalty might be assessed related to a position on a tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The tax advisor may not sign a return if the possibility of a penalty exists and the tax position is not disclosed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The tax advisor should advise the taxpayer to disclose the position on the tax return, but the taxpayer is responsible for deciding whether and how to disclose.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tax advisor should not recommend a position that could possibly result in a taxpayer penalty.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tax advisor is responsible for disclosing the position on the tax return, with or without the taxpayer's permission.

questions.explanation:
Under the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services on tax return positions, when recommending a position or preparing a return, a member should advise the taxpayer of any penalties reasonably likely to apply to the position and of any opportunity to avoid those penalties through disclosure. The taxpayer, not the tax advisor, has the responsibility for deciding whether and how to disclose.

A member may sign a return without disclosure if the position meets the applicable standard (for example, substantial authority), even if a penalty is possible. The standards do not prohibit recommending any position that could possibly result in a penalty. The tax advisor is not responsible for disclosing the position without the taxpayer's permission.
questions.explanationJa:
AICPAの税務業務基準（SSTS：申告ポジション）では、ポジションの推奨や申告書の作成に当たり、そのポジションに適用される可能性が合理的に高い罰則と、開示によって罰則を回避できる機会を納税者に助言すべきとされる。開示するかどうか、どのように開示するかを決める責任は納税者にある。

ポジションが適用基準（例えば相当の根拠：substantial authority）を満たしていれば、罰則の可能性があっても開示なしで署名できる。罰則の可能性があるポジションの推奨が一律に禁止されているわけではない。納税者の許可なく税務アドバイザーが開示する責任も無い。
references: AICPA SSTS — Tax Return Positions (former SSTS No. 1)
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2016 Recently Released Q.15 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: With respect to any given tax return, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More than one person may be deemed to be a preparer of a tax return.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The final reviewer of a tax return is automatically considered the preparer of the return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only one person may be deemed to be a preparer of a tax return.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The two individuals who have done the most work in preparing the return will be deemed to be the only preparers.

questions.explanation:
A tax return preparer under IRC §7701(a)(36) and Treas. Reg. §301.7701-15 is any person who prepares for compensation, or employs others to prepare, all or a substantial portion of a return. Because each person who prepares a substantial portion can qualify, more than one person may be deemed a preparer of the same return (for example, the signing preparer and a nonsigning preparer who prepared a substantial schedule).

The statement that only one person may be a preparer is incorrect for the same reason, and the statement limiting preparers to the two individuals who did the most work has no basis in the regulations. A final reviewer is not automatically a preparer; preparer status depends on preparing or being primarily responsible for a substantial portion of the return, not merely on reviewing it.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §7701(a)(36)とTreas. Reg. §301.7701-15では、報酬を得て申告書の全部または相当部分を作成する者（または作成させるために他者を雇う者）が申告書作成者である。相当部分を作成した者はそれぞれ該当しうるため、1つの申告書について複数の者が作成者とみなされることがある（署名作成者と、重要な明細を作成した非署名作成者など）。

作成者は1人だけという記述は同じ理由で誤りで、最も多く作業した2人だけが作成者になるという規定もない。最終レビュー担当者が自動的に作成者になるわけではなく、相当部分を作成したか、その主たる責任を負うかで判断する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.1 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Which agency is responsible for determining the continuing professional education requirements for licensed CPAs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Securities and Exchange Commission.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The board of accountancy for the state in which the licensed CPA practices.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The National Association of State Boards of Accountancy.

questions.explanation:
CPA licenses are issued and regulated by each state's board of accountancy. The board of the state in which the CPA is licensed sets the continuing professional education (CPE) requirements that must be met to renew and maintain the license, and it disciplines licensees who do not comply.

The Securities and Exchange Commission regulates securities markets and auditors of public companies but does not license CPAs. The American Institute of Certified Public Accountants sets CPE requirements for its own membership, not for licensure. The National Association of State Boards of Accountancy develops model standards (such as the CPE standards it issues jointly with the AICPA) but has no authority to impose them; each state board adopts its own rules.
questions.explanationJa:
CPAの免許は各州の会計士委員会（state board of accountancy）が発行・規制する。免許の更新・維持に必要な継続的専門研修（CPE）の要件は、そのCPAが免許を受けて業務を行う州の会計士委員会が定め、違反者の懲戒も行う。

SECは証券市場と上場会社の監査人を規制するが、CPA免許は扱わない。AICPAが定めるCPE要件は会員資格のためのもので、免許の要件ではない。NASBAはモデル基準を作成するが、それを強制する権限はなく、各州の委員会が自らの規則を定める。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.2 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A husband prepared his own tax return as married filing separately. His wife hired a CPA to prepare her tax return as married filing separately and asked the CPA not to disclose the information to anyone. The CPA was not retained by the husband for any tax work. The husband believed that his wife's tax return was negligently prepared and that he was financially harmed. He hired an attorney, without his wife's consent, to pursue a negligence claim against the CPA. The CPA hired an attorney to defend against the negligence claim. To which party, if any, may the CPA disclose the wife's tax return information without the wife's consent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The husband, for the evaluation of the negligence claim.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA's attorney, for the evaluation of the negligence claim.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The husband's attorney, for the evaluation of the negligence claim.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No one, because all disclosures must be made with the wife's consent.

questions.explanation:
IRC §7216 prohibits a tax return preparer from disclosing or using tax return information without the taxpayer's consent, subject to exceptions in Treas. Reg. §301.7216-2. One exception permits a preparer to disclose return information to the preparer's own attorney to obtain legal advice and to defend against a claim or proceeding relating to the preparer's services. The CPA may therefore give the wife's return information to the CPA's attorney so the attorney can evaluate and defend the negligence claim.
