The husband was not a client of the CPA and filed separately, so disclosure to him is not permitted without the wife's consent. The husband's attorney represents the adverse party and has no right to the information outside formal legal process. The statement that no one may receive the information without consent is incorrect because the regulations allow disclosure to the preparer's own counsel for this purpose.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §7216は、申告書作成者が納税者の同意なく申告書情報を開示・使用することを禁じるが、Treas. Reg. §301.7216-2に例外がある。その一つとして、作成者は自らの業務に関する請求・手続きに対応し法的助言を得るため、自分の弁護士に申告書情報を開示できる。したがってCPAは、過失請求の検討・防御のために妻の申告書情報を自らの弁護士に開示できる。

夫はCPAの顧客ではなく別々に申告しているため、妻の同意なく夫に開示することはできない。夫の弁護士は相手方の代理人であり、正式な法的手続きによらずに情報を受け取る権利はない。誰にも開示できないという記述は、この目的での自らの弁護士への開示が認められているため誤りである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.3 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: While reviewing a new client's prior-year tax returns, a CPA became aware that the client did not properly file all required federal income tax returns. Under Treasury Circular 230, what should the CPA do in this situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Notify the AICPA of the situation and request a ruling of continuance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Notify the Internal Revenue Service of the client's noncompliance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resign from the engagement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Advise the client of the consequences of the noncompliance.

questions.explanation:
Circular 230 §10.21 provides that a practitioner who knows that a client has not complied with the revenue laws, or has made an error in or omission from a return, must advise the client promptly of the noncompliance, error, or omission and of the consequences under the Code and regulations.

Circular 230 does not require the practitioner to notify the IRS of the client's noncompliance; doing so without consent would also breach confidentiality. Resignation is not required by §10.21 (although withdrawal may be considered if the client refuses to correct the problem), and the AICPA has no role in issuing a "ruling of continuance."
questions.explanationJa:
Circular 230 §10.21により、実務家は顧客が税法を遵守していないこと、または申告書の誤り・漏れを知った場合、その事実と、IRCおよび規則上の結果を速やかに顧客に助言しなければならない。

Circular 230は顧客の不遵守をIRSに通知することを求めておらず、同意なく通知すれば守秘義務にも反する。§10.21は辞任を求めておらず（顧客が是正を拒む場合に辞任を検討することはありうる）、AICPAに「継続の裁定」を求める手続きも存在しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.21 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A tax preparer filed a return for a taxpayer and used the taxpayer's detailed check register containing both business and personal expenses. If the tax preparer knowingly included personal expenses as deductible business expenses on the taxpayer's business, then the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tax preparer will be liable only for penalties for taking an unreasonable position that led to an understatement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Taxpayer will be liable for penalties for taking an unreasonable position that led to an understatement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tax preparer will be liable for penalties arising from an understatement due to willful or reckless conduct.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taxpayer will be liable for penalties attributable to transactions lacking economic substance.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6694(b), a tax return preparer is subject to a penalty for an understatement of liability due to willful or reckless conduct, including a willful attempt to understate the liability or a reckless or intentional disregard of rules or regulations. Knowingly deducting personal expenses as business expenses is willful conduct, so the preparer is liable for the §6694(b) penalty (the greater of $5,000 or 75% of the income derived from the return).

The §6694(a) unreasonable-position penalty covers positions lacking substantial authority or a reasonable basis; it does not describe knowing misconduct, and the preparer's liability is not limited to it. The facts address the preparer's knowing conduct, not a position taken by the taxpayer, and nothing in the facts involves a transaction lacking economic substance (§6662(b)(6)).
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §6694(b)により、申告書作成者が故意または重大な過失（willful or reckless conduct）によって税額を過少申告させた場合、ペナルティが科される（$5,000と当該申告書から得た報酬の75%のいずれか大きい額）。私的な支出を事業経費と知りながら計上するのは故意の行為なので、作成者は§6694(b)のペナルティを負う。

§6694(a)の不合理なポジションに対するペナルティは、相当な根拠や合理的根拠を欠くポジションを対象とするもので、故意の不正を表すものではなく、作成者の責任がそれに限られることもない。問題文は作成者の故意の行為を述べており、納税者が取ったポジションや経済的実体を欠く取引（§6662(b)(6)）に関する事実はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.22 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: To whom must a CPA pay license fees in order to maintain a CPA license?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The state board of accountancy of the CPA's state of licensure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The state society of certified public accountants of the CPA's state of licensure.

questions.explanation:
A CPA license is granted, renewed, and regulated by the state board of accountancy of the CPA's state of licensure. License and renewal fees are paid to that state board as a condition of maintaining the license.

The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board registers and inspects firms that audit public companies but does not license individual CPAs. The American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and state societies of CPAs are voluntary professional membership organizations; their dues relate to membership, not to holding a license.
questions.explanationJa:
CPA免許は、免許を受けた州の会計士委員会（state board of accountancy）が付与・更新・規制する。免許の維持のための手数料・更新料はその州の委員会に支払う。

PCAOBは上場会社を監査する事務所の登録・検査を行うが、個人のCPA免許は扱わない。AICPAと州のCPA協会は任意加入の職業団体であり、その会費は会員資格のためのもので免許とは関係がない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.23 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: An IRS agent has sent a 30-day letter reflecting a proposed adjustment to increase a client's taxable income in three prior years. The CPA and the client have reviewed the proposed changes and agree with the proposed adjustment. What would be the CPA's most appropriate recommendation to the client?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accept the proposed IRS changes and pay any deficiency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pay the tax, then file an appeal with the IRS Appeals Division.

choices.label: C
choices.text: File an offer in compromise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: File an amended federal tax return along with payment of any deficiency.

questions.explanation:
A 30-day letter proposes adjustments after an examination and gives the taxpayer 30 days to agree or to request a conference with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals. When the taxpayer agrees with the adjustments, the appropriate course is to accept them by signing the agreement form (such as Form 870, a waiver of restrictions on assessment under IRC §6213(d)) and pay the resulting deficiency, which also stops further interest from accruing.

An appeal is for taxpayers who disagree with the proposed adjustments, so paying and then appealing makes no sense when the client agrees. An offer in compromise is used when there is doubt as to liability or collectibility or for effective tax administration, not to settle an agreed deficiency the client can pay. Filing amended returns is unnecessary because the examination already determines the adjustments; agreeing to the 30-day letter closes the matter.
questions.explanationJa:
30日レター（30-day letter）は、税務調査後に更正案を示し、30日以内に同意するかIRS不服審査部（Independent Office of Appeals）との協議を求めるかを選ばせる通知である。納税者が更正案に同意する場合は、同意書（IRC §6213(d)の賦課制限の放棄であるForm 870など）に署名して受け入れ、追徴税額を納付するのが適切で、納付により以後の利息の発生も止まる。

不服申立ては更正案に同意しない納税者のための手続きなので、同意しているのに納付後に不服申立てをする意味はない。オファー・イン・コンプロマイズは税額や徴収可能性に疑義がある場合などに使うもので、同意済みで納付可能な追徴税額の決着には用いない。調査で更正内容がすでに確定しているので修正申告は不要であり、30日レターに同意すれば手続きは終わる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.17 (AICPA No. 66277)

questions.stem: A statutory notice of deficiency explains that the taxpayer has 90 days to either pay the deficiency or else to file a

choices.label: A
choices.text: Claim for refund.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Petition with the U.S. Tax Court.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protest and request a conference with an appeals officer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Petition with the taxpayer's U.S. District Court.

questions.explanation:
A statutory notice of deficiency (the 90-day letter) is issued under IRC §6212. Within 90 days of its mailing (150 days if addressed outside the U.S.), the taxpayer may file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court without paying the deficiency (IRC §6213(a)); otherwise the IRS may assess the tax.

A claim for refund is used after the tax is paid, and a refund suit in the U.S. District Court likewise requires payment first, so neither is the alternative offered by the 90-day letter. A protest and request for an Appeals conference is the response to the 30-day letter, which comes before the statutory notice of deficiency.
questions.explanationJa:
法定の不足額通知（90日レター）は IRC §6212 に基づき発行される。納税者は郵送から90日以内（米国外宛ては150日）に、不足額を納付せずに租税裁判所（U.S. Tax Court）へ申立てができる（IRC §6213(a)）。申立てがなければIRSは賦課できる。

還付請求は納付後に行う手続きで、連邦地方裁判所での訴訟も先に納付が必要なため、90日レターが示す選択肢ではない。不服申立て（protest）と不服審査部（Appeals）との協議の請求は、法定不足額通知の前に届く30日レターへの対応である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.1 (AICPA No. 71995)

questions.stem: A taxpayer contemplates entering into a complex transaction. The taxpayer wants assurance that there will be no adverse tax effects from the transaction. The taxpayer should apply for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Technical advice memorandum (TAM).

choices.label: B
choices.text: General counsel memorandum (GCM).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Revenue ruling.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Private letter ruling (PLR).

questions.explanation:
A private letter ruling (PLR) is a written statement issued by the IRS National Office to a taxpayer, in response to the taxpayer's request, that interprets and applies the tax law to the taxpayer's specific proposed transaction. It gives the requesting taxpayer advance assurance of the tax consequences, provided the facts are as represented (Treas. Reg. §601.201; the annual revenue procedure, e.g., Rev. Proc. 2026-1).

A technical advice memorandum is requested by IRS personnel during an examination or appeal of a completed transaction, not by a taxpayer planning a transaction. A general counsel memorandum is an internal IRS Chief Counsel document, not something a taxpayer applies for. A revenue ruling is published guidance of general application, not a response to one taxpayer's request about its own transaction.
questions.explanationJa:
プライベート・レター・ルーリング（PLR）は、納税者の申請に基づき IRS 本庁が、その納税者が予定する特定の取引に税法をどう適用するかを書面で示すもので、申請どおりの事実であれば申請者は事前に税務上の取扱いの確証を得られる（Treas. Reg. §601.201、毎年公表される Rev. Proc. 2026-1 など）。

技術的助言メモ（TAM）は、完了した取引の調査・不服審査の過程で IRS 職員が求めるもので、取引を計画中の納税者が申請するものではない。General counsel memorandum は IRS 首席法律顧問室の内部文書で、納税者が申請するものではない。Revenue ruling は一般に適用される公表された指針で、個々の納税者の取引に対する回答ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.2 (AICPA No. 59001)

questions.stem: If a CPA recklessly departs from the standards of due care when conducting an audit, the CPA will be liable to third parties who are unknown to the CPA under the law of

choices.label: A
choices.text: Strict liability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breach of contract.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Negligence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gross negligence.

questions.explanation:
Under common law, a CPA who is merely negligent is generally liable only to the client and to limited classes of third parties (privity, known users or foreseen users, depending on the jurisdiction). A CPA who acts with reckless disregard for professional standards commits gross negligence (constructive fraud), and liability for gross negligence or fraud extends to all reasonably foreseeable third parties, including those unknown to the CPA (Ultramares Corp. v. Touche).

Strict liability does not apply to professional services; liability depends on fault. Breach of contract requires privity, which unknown third parties lack. Ordinary negligence generally does not extend liability to third parties who are unknown to the CPA.
questions.explanationJa:
コモンロー上、単なる過失（ordinary negligence）の CPA は、原則として依頼人と限られた範囲の第三者（州により契約関係者、既知の利用者、予見された利用者）にのみ責任を負う。職業上の基準を無謀に無視した場合は重過失（gross negligence、擬制詐欺）となり、重過失や詐欺の責任は CPA が知らない第三者を含む合理的に予見可能なすべての第三者に及ぶ（Ultramares 事件）。

専門的役務には無過失責任（strict liability）は適用されない。契約違反には契約関係（privity）が必要で、未知の第三者にはない。通常の過失では CPA が知らない第三者にまで責任は及ばないのが原則である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.1 (AICPA No. 56475)

questions.stem: Which of the following defenses is likely to be successful in a suit alleging negligence by a CPA?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Due care.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ignorance of the law.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lack of intent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lack of mental capacity.

questions.explanation:
Negligence requires a duty, a breach of that duty (failure to exercise the care of a reasonably competent professional), causation and damages. A CPA who shows that the work was performed with due care, consistent with professional standards, defeats the breach element and therefore successfully defends against a negligence claim (Restatement (Second) of Torts §299A).

Ignorance of the law is not a defense; professionals are expected to know the applicable rules. Lack of intent is irrelevant because negligence does not require intent. Lack of mental capacity is not a recognized defense for a professional who undertakes an engagement.
questions.explanationJa:
過失責任の成立には、注意義務、その違反（合理的な専門家としての注意を尽くさなかったこと）、因果関係、損害が必要である。CPA が職業上の基準に従い正当な注意（due care）をもって業務を行ったことを示せば、義務違反の要件が否定され、過失の訴えに対する防御が成功する（Restatement (Second) of Torts §299A）。

法の不知は抗弁にならず、専門家は適用される規則を知っていることが前提とされる。過失は故意を要件としないので、故意がないことは無関係である。業務を引き受けた専門家にとって、精神的能力の欠如は認められた抗弁ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.2 (AICPA No. 57871)

questions.stem: Which of the following situations would most likely be a violation of the Treasury Circular 230 solicitation guidelines by a CPA, assuming that there are no violations of federal or state laws or other rules?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The CPA sends unsolicited e-mails to potential clients guaranteeing tax refunds from the Internal Revenue Service.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA mails solicitation letters, clearly identified as such, to randomly selected business firms from a local directory, disclosing how the firms were selected to be contacted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The CPA records a radio advertising broadcast that fails to disclose the fee charged for an initial consultation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The CPA advertises in a local newspaper as providing accounting and tax services without disclosing fee information.

questions.explanation:
Circular 230 §10.30(a)(1) prohibits a practitioner from using any form of public communication or private solicitation containing a false, fraudulent, coercive, misleading or deceptive statement or claim. Guaranteeing tax refunds from the IRS is a misleading claim, because no practitioner can guarantee the outcome, so the unsolicited e-mails guaranteeing refunds violate the solicitation rules.

An uninvited solicitation is not prohibited by Circular 230 unless it violates Federal or State law or other applicable rule (§10.30(a)(2)), and the question assumes no such violation; the clearly identified letters to randomly selected local firms contain no false or misleading claim. Circular 230 permits but does not require the publication of fee information (§10.30(b)), so a radio advertisement or newspaper advertisement that does not disclose fees is not a violation.
questions.explanationJa:
Circular 230 §10.30(a)(1) は、虚偽・詐欺的・強迫的・誤解を招く・欺瞞的な表示を含む広告や勧誘を禁じている。IRS からの還付を保証することは、結果を保証できる実務家はいないため誤解を招く表示であり、還付を保証する勧誘メールは勧誘規定に違反する。

Circular 230 は、連邦法・州法その他の適用規則に違反しない限り、依頼されていない勧誘そのものを禁じていない（§10.30(a)(2)）。本問は違反がないと仮定しており、勧誘と明示して地元の企業へ無作為に送る手紙には虚偽や誤解を招く表示もない。報酬情報の公表は認められているが義務ではない（§10.30(b)）ので、報酬を開示しないラジオ広告や新聞広告は違反ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.1 (AICPA No. 68479)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding a tax return preparer's penalty for aiding and abetting the understatement of a tax liability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The penalty applies to a person who provides only clerical assistance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The penalty does not apply if another penalty is assessed with respect to the same action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The taxpayer must have knowledge of the action causing the penalty for the penalty to apply.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The penalty applies to a return preparer who knows about and does not prevent the actions of a subordinate who understates the tax liability.

questions.explanation:
IRC §6701 imposes a penalty on any person who aids or assists in the preparation of any portion of a return or other document, knowing that it will be used in connection with a material tax matter and will result in an understatement of another person's tax liability. Under §6701(c), a person is treated as procuring an act if the person knows of, and does not attempt to prevent, participation by a subordinate in such an act; therefore the penalty applies to a preparer who knows about and does not prevent a subordinate's actions.

A person who furnishes only typing, reproducing or other mechanical (clerical) assistance is not treated as aiding or assisting (§6701(e)). The §6701 penalty is in addition to other penalties; it is the §6694 preparer penalty that is not imposed when the §6701 penalty is assessed for the same document (§6701(f)), not the reverse. The penalty applies whether or not the taxpayer has knowledge of or consents to the understatement (§6701(d)).
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §6701 は、申告書等の一部の作成を援助し、それが重要な税務事項に使われ他者の税額の過少申告につながることを知っている者に罰則を課す。§6701(c) により、部下がそのような行為に関与していることを知りながら防止しようとしない者も、その行為をさせたものとして扱われる。したがって、部下の過少申告を知りながら防止しない申告書作成者には罰則が適用される。

タイピングや複写などの機械的（事務的）な補助だけを行った者は援助したとは扱われない（§6701(e)）。§6701 の罰則は他の罰則に追加して課されるもので、同じ書類について §6701 の罰則が課された場合に課されないのは §6694 の作成者罰則の方である（§6701(f)）。納税者が過少申告を知っていたか、同意していたかにかかわらず罰則は適用される（§6701(d)）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.2 (AICPA No. 68199)

questions.stem: A tax return preparer is researching authorities to support a position of deferral of gain taken on the disposal of an asset. Which of the following will provide the highest authority for this position?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A conclusion reached in a legal periodical.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An opinion rendered by a tax professional.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A private letter ruling issued to another taxpayer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A temporary regulation issued by the Treasury Department.

questions.explanation:
Treasury regulations, including temporary regulations, are issued under the Treasury's statutory authority (IRC §7805) and have the force and effect of law until withdrawn or until they expire. In the hierarchy of tax authority they rank just below the Internal Revenue Code and treaties, so a temporary regulation provides the strongest support of the items listed.

A conclusion reached in a legal periodical is secondary source material; it is not authority at all for purposes of the substantial authority standard. An opinion rendered by a tax professional likewise is not authority. A private letter ruling issued to another taxpayer may be cited as substantial authority but may not be relied upon as precedent by anyone other than the taxpayer to whom it was issued (IRC §6110(k)(3)), so it ranks well below a regulation.
questions.explanationJa:
財務省規則（暫定規則を含む）はIRC §7805の授権に基づいて発出され、撤回または失効するまで法的拘束力を持つ。税務上の権威の序列ではIRC・租税条約に次ぐ位置にあり、選択肢の中では最も強い根拠になる。

法律雑誌の結論は二次資料であり、substantial authority の判断上の権威ではない。税務専門家の意見も権威ではない。他の納税者に発行されたプライベート・レター・ルーリングは、発行を受けた本人以外は先例として依拠できない（IRC §6110(k)(3)）ため、規則より大きく劣る。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.3 (AICPA No. 89218)

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a 90-day letter proposing a deficiency of $28,000. The taxpayer's CPA told the taxpayer that a client with similar circumstances successfully sustained such a position in the Small Claims Division of the U.S. Tax Court. If the taxpayer decides to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court, what is the significance of the success of the CPA's other client in sustaining the position in the Small Claims Division?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is little significance since decisions in the Small Claims Division of the U.S. Tax Court lack precedential value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The decision is significant because it can be used as a precedent for other taxpayers' appeals to the Small Claims Division, but not to the formal U.S. Tax Court.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The decision is significant because it can be used as a precedent in an appeal to the U.S. District Court, but only if a taxpayer pays the deficiency prior to commencing an appeal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The decision is significant because it can be used as a precedent for the taxpayer's appeal in any proceeding in the U.S. Tax Court provided that the taxpayer pays the deficiency prior to commencing an appeal.

questions.explanation:
A taxpayer may elect the small tax case procedure of the U.S. Tax Court when the amount in dispute is $50,000 or less for a tax year. Under IRC §7463(b), a decision entered in a small tax case may not be appealed and may not be treated as precedent for any other case. The other client's success therefore has little significance for this taxpayer.

Small case decisions are not precedent for other small case petitions, for regular Tax Court proceedings, or for proceedings in a U.S. District Court. Paying the deficiency before filing does not give a small case decision precedential value; prepayment only determines whether a refund suit may be brought in a District Court or the Court of Federal Claims.
questions.explanationJa:
係争額が課税年度あたり$50,000以下であれば、租税裁判所の少額事件手続を選択できる。IRC §7463(b)により、少額事件の判決は上訴できず、他の事件の先例にもならない。したがって他の顧客の勝訴は、この納税者にとってほとんど意味を持たない。

少額事件の判決は、他の少額事件、通常の租税裁判所の手続、連邦地方裁判所のいずれにおいても先例にならない。不足税額を先に納付しても先例性は生じない。先払いは、地方裁判所や連邦請求裁判所に還付訴訟を起こせるかどうかに関係するだけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.22 (AICPA No. 89214)

questions.stem: Which of the following situations could result in a preparer penalty assessed by the IRS?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Preparer does not sign the tax return.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Preparer inadvertently transposes two digits on a return, and the error results in an understatement of income by $90.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preparer takes an aggressive but realistic tax position that results in a decrease of tax.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taxpayer tells the preparer that the taxpayer's income is $40,000, whereas it is actually $60,000.

questions.explanation:
A tax return preparer who is required to sign a return and fails to do so is subject to a penalty for each failure unless the failure is due to reasonable cause and not willful neglect (IRC §6695(b)). Not signing the return can therefore result in a preparer penalty.

The IRC §6694(a) understatement penalty applies when the preparer knew or reasonably should have known that a position was unreasonable; an inadvertent transposition of two digits causing a $90 understatement is an isolated good-faith error and does not meet that standard. An aggressive position that is realistic (supported by substantial authority or by a reasonable basis with adequate disclosure) does not result in a §6694(a) penalty. A preparer may rely in good faith, without verification, on information furnished by the taxpayer (Treas. Reg. §1.6694-1(e)), so the taxpayer's misstatement of income does not by itself result in a preparer penalty.
questions.explanationJa:
署名が必要な申告書に署名しなかった申告書作成者には、正当な理由があり故意の怠慢でない場合を除き、1件ごとに罰則が科される（IRC §6695(b)）。したがって申告書への署名がないことは作成者罰則の対象になる。

§6694(a)の過少申告罰則は、作成者がそのポジションの不合理性を知っていたか知るべきであった場合に適用される。数字2桁を不注意で入れ替えて$90の過少申告になった単発の誤りはこれに当たらない。積極的でも現実的な（substantial authority がある、または reasonable basis があり開示した）ポジションは§6694(a)の罰則を受けない。作成者は納税者から提供された情報を、善意であれば検証せずに信頼できる（Treas. Reg. §1.6694-1(e)）ため、納税者が所得を偽って伝えたこと自体では作成者罰則は生じない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.2 (AICPA No. 64781)

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer rejected the IRS examiner's findings in an audit of the taxpayer's tax return. What will the IRS do in response to the taxpayer's rejection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Issue a 30-day letter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Begin immediate collection action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Issue a statutory notice of deficiency.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refer the case to the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.

questions.explanation:
When an examination ends with proposed adjustments that the taxpayer does not accept, the IRS sends a 30-day letter (Treas. Reg. §601.105(d)). The letter transmits the examination report and gives the taxpayer 30 days to agree, to request a conference with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals (filing a written protest where required), or to do nothing and receive a statutory notice of deficiency.

The IRS does not begin immediate collection; a deficiency in income tax generally may not be assessed or collected until a statutory notice of deficiency is issued and the period to petition the Tax Court has expired. The statutory notice of deficiency (90-day letter, IRC §6212) is issued later, if the taxpayer does not resolve the case after the 30-day letter. The case goes to the Independent Office of Appeals only if the taxpayer requests it in response to the 30-day letter; the IRS does not refer it automatically.
questions.explanationJa:
調査の結果、納税者が是正案を受け入れない場合、IRSは30日レター（30-day letter）を送付する（Treas. Reg. §601.105(d)）。調査報告書を添えて、30日以内に同意するか、IRS独立不服審査部（Independent Office of Appeals）での協議を求める（必要に応じて書面の異議申立てを出す）か、何もせず法定の不足額通知を待つかを選ばせるものである。

IRSが直ちに徴収を始めることはない。所得税の不足額は原則として、不足額通知の発出と租税裁判所への提訴期間の経過までは賦課・徴収できない。法定の不足額通知（90日レター、IRC §6212）は、30日レターの後も解決しない場合に後から発出される。不服審査部への移送は、納税者が30日レターに応じて請求した場合に行われるもので、IRSが自動的に回すものではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.20 (AICPA No. 502531)

questions.stem: Sumner is an accountant accused of negligence by a client. Which of the following defenses should Sumner argue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Actual fraud was lacking.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The negligence was not the proximate cause of the client's losses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contributory negligence negates liability for a client's losses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scienter was lacking.

questions.explanation:
To recover for negligence, the client must prove that the accountant owed a duty of care, breached that duty, and that the breach was the proximate (legal) cause of the client's damages. Showing that the negligence was not the proximate cause of the client's losses defeats an essential element of the claim, so it is the defense Sumner should argue.

Lack of actual fraud is irrelevant, because negligence does not require proof of fraud. Lack of scienter (intent to deceive or reckless disregard) likewise is a defense only to fraud claims, not to negligence. Contributory negligence is not a reliable defense: most jurisdictions have replaced it with comparative negligence, under which the client's own negligence merely reduces the damages rather than negating the accountant's liability.
questions.explanationJa:
過失による損害賠償を請求するには、依頼人は、会計士の注意義務の存在、その違反、そして違反が依頼人の損害の近因（proximate cause）であることを立証しなければならない。過失が損害の近因ではないことを示せば請求の必須要件が欠けるので、Sumnerはこの抗弁を主張すべきである。

実際の詐欺がないことは、過失責任には詐欺の立証が不要なので抗弁にならない。scienter（欺く意図・重大な無謀）の欠如も詐欺の請求に対する抗弁であり、過失には関係しない。寄与過失は、多くの法域で比較過失に置き換えられており、依頼人の過失は賠償額を減らすだけで会計士の責任を否定しないため、確実な抗弁にならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.22 (AICPA No. 73485)
